commands.name: triangle
commands.doc:
Draw a triangle.

Fill the triangle if *filled* is set to `#t`.

The appearance can be controlled with properties `extroversion`,
`font-size`, and `thickness`.

```lilypond
\markup {
  \triangle ##t
  \triangle ##f
  \override #'(font-size . 5)
  \override #'(thickness . 5) {
    \override #'(extroversion . 1)
    \triangle ##f
    \override #'(extroversion . -1)
    \triangle ##f
  }
}
```

commands.name: tuplet
commands.doc:
Scale the given *music* to tuplets.

*ratio* is a fraction that specifies how many notes are played in place of
the nominal value: it will be 3/2 for triplets, namely three notes being played
in place of two.

If the optional duration *tuplet-span* is specified, it is used instead of
`tupletSpannerDuration` for grouping the tuplets.  For example,

```
\tuplet 3/2 4 { c8 c c c c c }
```

results in two groups of three tuplets, each group lasting for a quarter note.

commands.name: tupletSpan
commands.doc:
Set `tupletSpannerDuration` to the duration *tuplet-span*.

This context property is the length into which `\tuplet` without an
explicit tuplet span argument of its own will group its tuplets.  To revert to
the default of not subdividing the contents of a `\tuplet` command without
an explicit tuplet span argument, use

```
\tupletSpan \default
```

commands.name: tweak
commands.doc:
Add a tweak to *music*.

Layout objects created by *music* get their property *prop* set to
*value*.  If *prop* has the form `*Grob*@/.*property*`,
like with

```
\tweak Accidental.color #red cis'
```

an indirectly created grob (`Accidental` is caused by `NoteHead`) can
be tweaked; otherwise only directly created grobs are affected.

*prop* can contain additional elements in which case a nested
property (inside of an alist) is tweaked.

If *music* is an `event-chord`, every contained `rhythmic-event`
is tweaked instead.

commands.name: type
commands.doc: In a context definition: the translator group type.

commands.name: typewriter
commands.doc:
Print *arg* in typewriter.

This command sets the `font-family` property to `typewriter`, also
switching off the ‘liga’ OpenType feature to disable ligatures like ‘ff’ or
‘fi’.

```lilypond
\markup {
  "default fi ff"
  \hspace #2
  \typewriter "typewriter fi ff"
}
```

commands.name: unHideNotes
commands.expansion:
\revert Accidental.transparent
\revert Stem.transparent
\revert NoteHead.transparent
\revert NoteHead.no-ledgers
\revert Dots.transparent
\revert Rest.transparent
\revert TabNoteHead.transparent

commands.name: underline
commands.doc:
Underline *arg*.

This function looks at the property `thickness` to determine the line
thickness, at `offset` to determine the line's vertical offset from
*arg*, and at `underline-skip` to determine the distance of additional
lines from the others.

The `underline-shift` property is used to make subsequent calls work
correctly.  Overriding it makes little sense since it would end up adding the
provided value to the one of `offset`.

```lilypond
\markup \justify-line {
  \underline "underlined"
  \override #'(offset . 5)
  \override #'(thickness . 1)
  \underline "underlined"
  \override #'(offset . 1)
  \override #'(thickness . 5)
  \underline "underlined"
  \override #'(offset . 5)
  \override #'(underline-skip . 4)
  \underline \underline \underline "underlined thrice"
}
```

commands.name: undertie
commands.doc:
Print a tie under *arg*.

```lilypond
\markup \line {
  \undertie "undertied"
  \override #'((offset . 5) (thickness . 1))
  \undertie "undertied"
  \override #'((offset . 1) (thickness . 5))
  \undertie "undertied"
}
```

commands.name: undo
commands.doc:
Convert `\override` and `\set` in *music* to
`\revert` and `\unset`, respectively.

Any reverts and unsets already in *music* cause a warning.
Non-property-related music is ignored.

commands.name: unfoldRepeats
commands.doc:
Unfold `\repeat`.

This forces `\repeat volta`, `\repeat tremolo` or `\repeat
percent` commands in *music* to be interpreted as `\repeat unfold`, if
specified in the optional symbol-list *types*.  The default for *types*
is an empty list, which forces any of those commands in *music* to be
interpreted as `\repeat unfold`.  Possible entries are `volta`,
`tremolo` or `percent`.  Multiple entries are possible.

commands.name: unfolded
commands.doc: Mask *music* until the innermost enclosing repeat is unfolded.

commands.name: unless
unset
commands.doc: Returns a context property to its default: `\unset Staff.instrumentName`.

commands.name: upright
vcenter
commands.doc:
Align *arg* to its Y center.

```lilypond
\markup {
  one
  \vcenter two
  three
}
```

commands.name: verbatim-file
commands.doc:
Read the contents of file *name* and include it verbatim.

```lilypond
\markup {
  \verbatim-file "en/included/simple.ly"
}
```

Use `\withRelativeDir` as a prefix to *name* if the file should be
found relative to the input file.

commands.name: version
commands.doc: The LilyPond version the file was written for; `convert-ly` relies on it.

commands.name: versus
commands.doc:
Prepend character U+2123 (versicle) to the lyrics represented by
*music*.

commands.name: voices
commands.doc:
Specify voice order in simultaneous music.

This takes the key list *ids* of numbers (indicating the use of
`\voiceOne`…) or symbols (indicating voice names, typically
converted from strings by argument list processing) and assign the following
`\\`-separated music in *music* to contexts according to that list.
Named rather than numbered contexts can be used for continuing one voice (for
the sake of spanners and lyrics), usually requiring a `\voiceOne`-style
override at the beginning of the passage and a `\oneVoice` override at its
end.

The default

```
<< … \\ … \\ … >>
```

construct would correspond to

```
\voices 1,2,3 << … \\ … \\ … >>
```

commands.name: void
commands.doc:
Accept a Scheme argument *arg* and return a void expression.

Use this if you want to have a Scheme expression evaluated because of its side
effects but its return value being ignored.

commands.name: volta
commands.doc:
Mark *music* as being limited to the volte given in
*volta-numbers*.

This gets used when the innermost enclosing repeat is unfolded.  Volta number
begins at 1 and increases by 1 with each repetition.

commands.name: volta-number
commands.doc:
Set *arg* in a font appropriate for volta numbers.

```lilypond
\markup \volta-number "4."
```

commands.name: vshape
commands.doc:
Like `\shape`, but additionally show control points for ease of
tweaking.

commands.name: vspace
walkerHeads
commands.expansion: \set shapeNoteStyles = ##(doWalker reWalker miWalker faWalker solFunk laWalker tiWalker)

commands.name: walkerHeadsMinor
commands.expansion: \set shapeNoteStyles = ##(laWalker tiWalker doWalker reWalker miWalker faWalker solFunk)

commands.name: whiteout
commands.doc:
Provide a white background for *arg*.

The shape of the white background is determined by the `style` property.
The default is `box` which produces a rectangle.  `rounded-box`
produces a rounded rectangle, and `outline` approximates the outline of the
markup.

The color of the background can be controlled with the `color` property,
defaulting to `"white"`.

```lilypond
\markup {
  \combine
    \filled-box #'(-1 . 62) #'(-3 . 4) #1
    \override #'(line-width . 60)
      \fill-line {
        \override #'(thickness . 1.5)
          \whiteout box
        \override #'((style . rounded-box) (thickness . 3))
          \whiteout rounded-box
        \override #'((style . outline) (thickness . 3))
          \whiteout outline
        \override #'((color . "red") (style . outline))
          \whiteout red-outline
      }
}
```

commands.name: with
commands.doc: Settings for the context being created: `\new Staff \with { … }`.

commands.name: with-color
commands.doc:
Use color *col* to draw *arg*.

Coloring objects for valid color specifications.

```lilypond
\markup {
  \with-color #red red
  \hspace #2
  \with-color #green green
  \hspace #2
  \with-color "#0000ff" blue
}
```

commands.name: with-dimension
commands.doc:
Set the dimension of *arg* along *axis* to *val*.

If *axis* is equal to `X`, set the horizontal dimension.  If
*axis* is equal to `Y`, set the vertical dimension.

commands.name: with-dimension-from
commands.doc:
Print *arg2* but replace the dimension along *axis* with the one from
*arg1*.

If *axis* is set to `X`, replace the horizontal dimension.  If
*axis* is set to `Y`, replace the vertical dimension.

commands.name: with-dimensions
commands.doc:
Set the horizontal and vertical dimensions of *arg* to *x*
and *y*.

commands.name: with-dimensions-from
commands.doc: Print *arg2* with the horizontal and vertical dimensions of *arg1*.

commands.name: with-link
with-outline
commands.doc:
Print *arg* with the outline and dimensions of *outline*.

The outline is used by skylines to resolve collisions (not for whiteout).

commands.name: with-string-transformer
commands.doc:
Apply string transformer function *transformer* to *arg*.

Whenever a string is interpreted inside *arg*, function *transformer* is
called first, and its result is then interpreted.  The arguments passed to
*transformer* are the output definition, the property alist chain, and the
markup *arg*.  See New markup command definition about the two
first arguments.

```lilypond
\markup \with-string-transformer
  #(lambda (layout props str)
     (string-upcase str))
  \concat { "abc" \larger "def" }
```

commands.name: with-true-dimension
commands.doc:
Give *arg* its actual dimension (extent) on *axis*.

Sometimes, the extents of a markup's printed ink differs from the default
extents.  The main case is if glyphs are involved.  By default, the extents of a
glyph are based on the glyph's *metrics* (i.e., a default vertical and
horizontal size for the glyph), which, for various reasons, are often not
identical to its *bounding box* (i.e., the smallest rectangle that
completely encompasses the glyph's outline) -- in most cases, the outline
protrudes the box spanned up by the metrics.

```lilypond
\markup {
  text
  \fontsize #10
  \override #'((box-padding . 0) (thickness . 0.2))
  \box
    \musicglyph "scripts.trill"
  text
}
```

For purposes other than setting text, this behavior may not be wanted.
You can use `\with-@/true-@/dimension` in order to give the markup
its actual printed extent.

```lilypond
\markup {
  text
  \fontsize #10
  \override #'((box-padding . 0) (thickness . 0.2))
  \box
    \with-true-dimension #X
    \musicglyph "scripts.trill"
  text
}
```

commands.name: with-true-dimensions
commands.doc:
Give *arg* its actual dimensions (extents).

Calling

```
\markup \with-true-dimensions arg
```

is short for

```
\markup
  \with-true-dimension #X
  \with-true-dimension #Y
  arg
```

i.e., `\with-@/true-@/dimensions` has the effect of
`\with-@/true-@/dimension` on both axes.

commands.name: with-url
withMusicProperty
commands.doc: Set music property *sym* to *val* in *music*.

commands.name: withRelativeDir
commands.doc:
Prepend directory of current input file to string *file-name*.

Use this for markup commands that include files, and where such files
should be found relative to the input file.  Example:

```
\markup { \image #X #3 \withRelativeDir "test.png" }
```

commands.name: woodwind-diagram
commands.doc:
Make a woodwind-instrument diagram for *instrument* using
*user-draw-commands*.

*user-draw-commands* is a list of alists, specifying the left-hand keys, the
elements on the central column, and the right-hand keys.  For example, this
diagram

```lilypond
\markup \woodwind-diagram
  #'oboe #'((lh . (d ees))
            (cc . (five3qT1q))
            (rh . (gis)))
```

shows an oboe with the left-hand d key, left-hand ees key, and right-hand
gis key depressed, while the five-hole of the central column effectuating a
trill between 1/4 and 3/4 is closed.

The following instruments are supported:

-
piccolo
-
flute
-
oboe
-
clarinet
-
bass-clarinet
-
saxophone
-
bassoon
-
contrabassoon

To see all of the callable keys for a given instrument, include the function
call `(print-keys '*instrument*)` in your `.ly` file, where
*instrument* is the instrument whose keys you want to print.

Certain keys allow for special configurations.  The entire gamut of
configurations possible is as follows:

- `1q`:
1/4 covered
- `1h`:
1/2 covered
- `3q`:
3/4 covered
- `R`:
ring depressed
- `F`:
fully covered; the default if no state put

Additionally, these configurations can be used in trills.  So, for example,
`three3qTR` effectuates a trill between 3/4 full and ring depressed
on the three hole.  As another example, `threeRT` effectuates a trill
between R and open, whereas `threeTR` effectuates a trill between open
and shut.  To see all of the possibilities for all of the keys of a given
instrument, invoke `(print-keys-verbose '*instrument*)`.

Lastly, substituting an empty list for the pressed-key alist results in
a diagram with all of the keys drawn but none filled, for example

```lilypond
\markup \woodwind-diagram #'flute #'()
```

commands.name: wordwrap
commands.doc:
Print *args* as left-aligned lines.

This function provides simple word-wrap.  Use `\override #'(line-width
. *X*)` to set the line width; *X* is the number of staff spaces.

```lilypond
\markup {
  \wordwrap {
    Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipisicing elit,
    sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore
    magna aliqua.  Ut enim ad minim veniam, quis nostrud
    exercitation ullamco laboris nisi ut aliquip ex ea
    commodo consequat.
  }
}
```

The baseline of the output of `\wordwrap` is the baseline of its first
line.

commands.name: wordwrap-field
wordwrap-lines
commands.doc:
Print *args* as left-aligned lines.

Like `\wordwrap`, but return a list of lines instead of a single markup.
Use `\override-lines #'(line-width . *X*)` to set the line width,
where *X* is the number of staff spaces.

commands.name: wordwrap-string
commands.doc:
Print string *arg* as left-aligned lines.

Paragraphs are indicated by double newlines.  Use `\override #'(line-width
. *X*)` to set the line width; *X* is the number of staff spaces.

```lilypond
\markup {
  \override #'(line-width . 40)
  \wordwrap-string "Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet,
      consectetur adipisicing elit, sed do eiusmod tempor
      incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua.


      Ut enim ad minim veniam, quis nostrud exercitation
      ullamco laboris nisi ut aliquip ex ea commodo
      consequat.


      Excepteur sint occaecat cupidatat non proident,
      sunt in culpa qui officia deserunt mollit anim id
      est laborum"
}
```

The baseline of the output of `\wordwrap-string` is the baseline of its
first line.

commands.name: xNote
commands.doc: Print *note* with a cross-shaped note head.

contexts.name: ChoirStaff
contexts.doc:
Identical to `StaffGroup` except that the
contained staves are not connected vertically.

contexts.name: ChordGrid
contexts.doc:
Creates chord grid notation.  This context is always part of
a `ChordGridScore` context.

contexts.name: ChordGridScore
contexts.doc:
Top-level context replacing `Score` in chord grid notation.
Compared to `Score`, it uses proportional notation, and has a few other
settings like removing bar numbers.

contexts.name: ChordNames
contexts.doc: Typesets chord names.

contexts.name: CueVoice
contexts.doc:
A voice context used to render notes of a reduced size,
intended primarily for adding cue notes to a staff.  Usually left to be
created implicitly.

contexts.name: Devnull
contexts.doc:
Silently discard all musical information given to this
context.

contexts.name: DrumStaff
contexts.doc:
Handles typesetting for percussion.  Can contain
`DrumVoice`.

contexts.name: DrumVoice
contexts.doc: A voice on a percussion staff.

contexts.name: Dynamics
contexts.doc:
Holds a single line of dynamics centered between the staves
surrounding this context.

contexts.name: FiguredBass
contexts.doc:
The context in which `BassFigure` grobs are created
from input entered in `\figuremode` mode.

contexts.name: FretBoards
contexts.doc: A context for displaying fret diagrams.

contexts.name: Global
contexts.doc:
Hard coded entry point for LilyPond.  Usually not meant
to be modified directly.

contexts.name: GrandStaff
contexts.doc:
Connect staves vertically by adding a brace on the
left side.  The bar lines of the contained staves are connected
vertically, too.

contexts.name: GregorianTranscriptionLyrics
contexts.doc:
A lyrics context for notating Gregorian chant in
modern style.

contexts.name: GregorianTranscriptionStaff
contexts.doc: A staff for notating Gregorian chant in modern style.

contexts.name: GregorianTranscriptionVoice
contexts.doc: A voice for notating Gregorian chant in modern style.

contexts.name: InternalGregorianStaff
contexts.doc:
A kind of `Staff` with settings shared by
multiple variants of Gregorian chant notation.

contexts.name: InternalMensuralStaff
contexts.doc:
An kind of `Staff` with settings shared by
multiple variants of mensural notation.

contexts.name: KievanStaff
contexts.doc:
Same as `Staff` context, except that it is
accommodated for typesetting a piece in Kievan style.

contexts.name: KievanVoice
contexts.doc:
Same as `Voice` context, except that it is
accommodated for typesetting a piece in Kievan style.

contexts.name: Lyrics
contexts.doc:
Corresponds to a voice with lyrics.  Handles the
printing of a single line of lyrics.

contexts.name: MensuralStaff
contexts.doc:
Same as `Staff` context, except that it is
accommodated for typesetting a piece in mensural style.

contexts.name: MensuralVoice
contexts.doc:
Same as `Voice` context, except that it is
accommodated for typesetting a piece in mensural style.

contexts.name: NoteNames
contexts.doc: Typesets note names.

contexts.name: NullVoice
contexts.doc: For aligning lyrics without printing notes.

contexts.name: OneStaff
contexts.doc:
Provides a common axis for the contained staves,
making all of them appear in the same vertical space.  This can be
useful for typesetting staves of different types in immediate succession
or for temporarily changing the character of one staff or overlaying
it with a different one.  Often used with `\stopStaff` and
`\startStaff` for best results.

contexts.name: PetrucciStaff
contexts.doc:
A kind of `Staff` approximating the mensural
typesetting of Ottaviano Petrucci's *Harmonices Musices
Odhecaton* (Venice, 1501).

contexts.name: PetrucciVoice
contexts.doc:
A kind of `Voice` approximating the mensural
typesetting of Ottaviano Petrucci's *Harmonices Musices
Odhecaton* (Venice, 1501).

contexts.name: PianoStaff
contexts.doc:
Just like `GrandStaff`, but the staves are only removed
together, never separately.

contexts.name: RhythmicStaff
contexts.doc:
Like `Staff` but for printing rhythms.  Pitches are
ignored when engraving; the notes are printed on one line.  The MIDI
rendition retains pitches unchanged.

contexts.name: Score
contexts.doc:
This is the top-level notation context.  No
other context can contain a `Score` context.  This context
handles the administration of time signatures.  It also makes sure
that items such as clefs, time signatures, and key-signatures are
aligned across staves.

You cannot explicitly instantiate a `Score` context (since it
is not contained in any other context).  It is instantiated
automatically when an output definition (a `\score` or
`\layout` block) is processed.

Timing
An alias called `Timing` is established by the
`Timing_translator` in whatever context it is initialized, and
the timing variables are then copied from wherever `Timing`
had been previously established.  The alias at `Score` level
provides a target for initializing `Timing` variables in
layout definitions before any `Timing_translator` has been
run.

contexts.name: Staff
contexts.doc:
Handles clefs, bar lines, keys, accidentals.  It can contain
`Voice` contexts.

contexts.name: StaffGroup
contexts.doc:
Connect staves vertically by adding a bracket on the
left side.  The bar lines of the contained staves are connected
vertically, too.

contexts.name: StandaloneRhythmScore
contexts.doc:
A `Score`-level context for use by
`\markup \rhythm`.

contexts.name: StandaloneRhythmStaff
contexts.doc:
A `Staff`-level context for use by
`\markup \rhythm`.

contexts.name: StandaloneRhythmVoice
contexts.doc:
A `Voice`-level context for use by
`\markup \rhythm`.

contexts.name: TabStaff
contexts.doc:
Context for generating tablature.  It accepts only
`TabVoice` contexts and handles the line spacing, the tablature clef,
etc., properly.

contexts.name: TabVoice
contexts.doc:
The voice context used within a `TabStaff` context.
Usually left to be created implicitly.

contexts.name: VaticanaLyrics
contexts.doc:
Same as `Lyrics` context, except that it
provides a hyphenation style (a single, flush-left hyphen between
two syllables) as used in the notational style of *Editio Vaticana*.

contexts.name: VaticanaScore
contexts.doc:
Top-level context replacing `Score` for Gregorian chant
notated in Vaticana style.  Compared to `Score`, it changes the staff
line color to red, uses packed spacing, and removes bar numbers.

contexts.name: VaticanaStaff
contexts.doc:
Configure division commands such as `\section`
to create `Divisio` grobs rather than `BarLine` grobs.  This
does not affect measure bar lines or the properties of the grobs
themselves.

contexts.name: VaticanaVoice
contexts.doc:
A kind of `Voice` for typesetting Gregorian chant
in a notational style approximating *Editio Vaticana*.

contexts.name: Voice
contexts.doc:
Corresponds to a voice on a staff.  This context
handles the conversion of dynamic signs, stems, beams, super- and
subscripts, slurs, ties, and rests.

You have to instantiate this explicitly if you want to have
multiple voices on the same staff.

grobs.name: Accidental
grobs.doc:
An accidental.  Horizontal
padding and configuration between accidentals is controlled
by the AccidentalPlacement grob.

grobs.name: AccidentalCautionary
grobs.doc:
A cautionary accidental, normally
enclosed in parentheses.

grobs.name: AccidentalPlacement
grobs.doc:
In groups of Accidental
grobs, this auxiliary grob controls their horizontal padding and
configuration (which ones are placed more to left or to the
right).

grobs.name: AccidentalSuggestion
grobs.doc:
An annotational accidental as used
in *musica ficta*.  Normally positioned above a note.

grobs.name: Ambitus
grobs.doc:
An ambitus, giving the range of
pitches of a voice or instrument.  It aligns
AmbitusAccidental, AmbitusLine,
and AmbitusNoteHead horizontally and defines the
horizontal spacing from the ambitus to other items.

grobs.name: AmbitusAccidental
grobs.doc:
An accidental in an
Ambitus.

grobs.name: AmbitusLine
grobs.doc:
The vertical line in an
Ambitus.

grobs.name: AmbitusNoteHead
grobs.doc:
A note head in an
Ambitus.

grobs.name: ApproximatePitchNoteHead
grobs.doc:
A note head for a pitch that cannot be notated
with certainty.  See also NoteHead.

grobs.name: Arpeggio
grobs.doc:
An arpeggio line (normally a
vertical wiggle).  See also ChordBracket and ChordSlur.

grobs.name: BalloonText
grobs.doc:
A balloon text with a pointing
line to visually mark and annotate another grob.

grobs.name: BarLine
grobs.doc: A bar line.

grobs.name: BarNumber
grobs.doc:
An ordinary bar number.  Centered
bar numbers are managed separately with CenteredBarNumber
grobs.

grobs.name: BassFigure
grobs.doc:
A number in figured bass.  It can contain an
alteration as well.

grobs.name: BassFigureAlignment
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob to stack
several BassFigureLine grobs vertically.

grobs.name: BassFigureAlignmentPositioning
grobs.doc:
If figured bass is used in the
Staff context, this auxiliary grob groups all of the
figured bass notation and computes an offset from the staff via
side-positioning.

grobs.name: BassFigureBracket
grobs.doc:
Brackets around a figured bass
(or elements of it).

grobs.name: BassFigureContinuation
grobs.doc:
A horizontal line to indicate
that a number of a previous figured bass is continued in the
current figured bass.

grobs.name: BassFigureLine
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob providing a
baseline for bass figures that should be aligned
vertically.

grobs.name: Beam
grobs.doc: A beam.

grobs.name: BendAfter
grobs.doc:
A grob for displaying
*falls* and *doits*.

grobs.name: BendSpanner
grobs.doc:
A string bending as used in
tablature notation.

grobs.name: BreakAlignGroup
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob to group
several breakable items of the same type (clefs, time signatures,
etc.) across staves so that they will be aligned horizontally.
See also BreakAlignment.

grobs.name: BreakAlignment
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob that manages
the horizontal ordering of BreakAlignGroup grobs within a
NonMusicalPaperColumn grob (for example, whether the
time signature follows or precedes a bar line).

grobs.name: BreathingSign
grobs.doc: A breathing sign.

grobs.name: CaesuraScript
grobs.doc:
A script for `\caesura`, e.g.,
an outside-staff comma or a fermata over a bar line.

grobs.name: CenteredBarNumber
grobs.doc:
A centered bar number; see also
CenteredBarNumberLineSpanner.  Ordinary bar numbers are
managed with BarNumber grobs.

grobs.name: CenteredBarNumberLineSpanner
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob providing a
vertical baseline to align CenteredBarNumber grobs.

grobs.name: ChordBracket
grobs.doc:
A non-arpeggiato or non-divisi bracket.  See
also Arpeggio and ChordSlur.

grobs.name: ChordName
grobs.doc:
A stand-alone chord name.  For chord
names in chord grids, see GridChordName.

grobs.name: ChordSlur
grobs.doc: A vertical slur.  See also Arpeggio and ChordBracket.

grobs.name: ChordSquare
grobs.doc:
In a chord grid, this grob represents one chord
square.  It helps place GridChordName grobs, and draws lines to separate
them. Note that this grob only draws the diagonal lines in a square.  The borders
of the square are drawn by StaffSymbol and BarLine.

grobs.name: Clef
grobs.doc:
A clef.  See also
ClefModifier, CueClef, and CueEndClef.

grobs.name: ClefModifier
grobs.doc:
A grob that draws the clef
modifier (if present), in most cases the digit 8 below or
above the clef.  See also Clef, CueClef, and
CueEndClef.

grobs.name: ClusterSpanner
grobs.doc:
A cluster spanner.  The envelope
shape within the spanner is given by ClusterSpannerBeacon
grobs.

grobs.name: ClusterSpannerBeacon
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob to specify the
minimum and maximum pitch of a ClusterSpanner grob at a
given moment.

grobs.name: CodaMark
grobs.doc: A coda mark.

grobs.name: CombineTextScript
grobs.doc:
A grob for printing markup given
in the `soloText`, `soloIIText`, and `aDueText`
properties if automatic part combining is active.

grobs.name: ControlPoint
grobs.doc:
A visual representation of a
Bézier control point in ties and slurs.

grobs.name: ControlPolygon
grobs.doc:
A visual representation of a
Bézier control polygon as used in ties and slurs.

grobs.name: CueClef
grobs.doc:
A clef starting a cue.  See also
Clef, ClefModifier, and CueEndClef.

grobs.name: CueEndClef
grobs.doc:
A clef ending a cue.  See also
Clef, ClefModifier, and CueClef.

grobs.name: Custos
grobs.doc:
A custos, mainly used in older
notation like Gregorian chant.

grobs.name: Divisio
grobs.doc:
A structural divider in a chant,
often calling for a breath or caesura.

grobs.name: DotColumn
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob to align
stacked Dots grobs of dotted notes and chords.

grobs.name: Dots
grobs.doc:
The dot(s) of a dotted note.
See also DotColumn.

grobs.name: DoublePercentRepeat
grobs.doc:
A double-percent symbol for
repeating two bars.  See also DoublePercentRepeatCounter,
PercentRepeat, DoubleRepeatSlash, and
RepeatSlash.

grobs.name: DoublePercentRepeatCounter
grobs.doc:
A grob to print a counter for
DoublePercentRepeat grobs.

grobs.name: DoubleRepeatSlash
grobs.doc:
A double-percent symbol for
repeating patterns shorter than a single measure, and which
contain mixed durations.  See also PercentRepeat,
DoublePercentRepeat, and RepeatSlash.

grobs.name: DurationLine
grobs.doc:
A horizontal duration line,
continuing rhythmic items (usually note heads).

grobs.name: DynamicLineSpanner
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob providing a
vertical baseline to align successive dynamic grobs
(DynamicText, DynamicTextSpanner,
and Hairpin) within a staff.

grobs.name: DynamicText
grobs.doc:
A dynamic text item like ‘ff’
or ‘mp’.  See also DynamicLineSpanner.

grobs.name: DynamicTextSpanner
grobs.doc:
Dynamic text like ‘cresc’,
usually followed by a (dashed) line.  See also
DynamicLineSpanner and TextSpanner.

grobs.name: Episema
grobs.doc:
An *episema* line (over a
group of notes).  Used in Gregorian chant.

grobs.name: FingerGlideSpanner
grobs.doc:
A line connecting two
Fingering, StringNumber or StrokeFinger grobs, usually
indicating a gliding finger, the same string, or the same stroking finger for
stringed instruments .

grobs.name: Fingering
grobs.doc:
A fingering symbol (usually a
digit).  See also FingeringColumn and
StrokeFinger.

grobs.name: FingeringColumn
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob to align
stacked Fingering grobs.

grobs.name: Flag
grobs.doc:
A flag (in the musical
sense).

grobs.name: Footnote
grobs.doc:
A footnote mark (usually a
number) with a pointing line attached to another grob.

grobs.name: FretBoard
grobs.doc: A fretboard diagram.

grobs.name: Glissando
grobs.doc: A glissando line.

grobs.name: GraceSpacing
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob to handle
(horizontal) spacing of grace notes.  See also
NoteSpacing, StaffSpacing,
and SpacingSpanner.

grobs.name: GridChordName
grobs.doc: A chord name in a chord grid.

grobs.name: GridLine
grobs.doc:
A vertical line between staves,
indicating rhythmic synchronization.  See also
GridPoint.

grobs.name: GridPoint
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob marking a
start or end point for a GridLine grob.

grobs.name: Hairpin
grobs.doc:
A hairpin.  See also
DynamicLineSpanner.

grobs.name: HorizontalBracket
grobs.doc:
A horizontal bracket between
notes.  See also HorizontalBracketText and
MeasureSpanner.

grobs.name: HorizontalBracketText
grobs.doc:
Text (markup) for a
HorizontalBracket grob.

grobs.name: InstrumentName
grobs.doc:
An instrument name, usually
displayed to the left of a staff.

grobs.name: InstrumentSwitch
grobs.doc:
This grob is deprecated.  Do
not use it.

grobs.name: JumpScript
grobs.doc:
A grob to display a ‘point of
departure’ like *D.C. al fine*.

grobs.name: KeyCancellation
grobs.doc:
A key cancellation, normally
consisting of naturals, to be displayed (if necessary) immediately
before a KeySignature grob if the key changes.

grobs.name: KeySignature
grobs.doc:
A key signature.  See also
KeyCancellation.

grobs.name: KievanLigature
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob to handle a
melisma (ligature) as used in Kievan square notation.  See also
MensuralLigature, VaticanaLigature, and
LigatureBracket.

grobs.name: LaissezVibrerTie
grobs.doc:
A laissez-vibrer tie (i.e., a
tie from a note into nothing).  See also
LaissezVibrerTieColumn, RepeatTie, and
Tie.

grobs.name: LaissezVibrerTieColumn
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob to determine
direction and shape of stacked LaissezVibrerTie
grobs.

grobs.name: LedgerLineSpanner
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob to manage
ledger lines of a whole staff.

grobs.name: LeftEdge
grobs.doc:
The left edge of a staff.  Useful
as an anchor point for other grobs.

grobs.name: LigatureBracket
grobs.doc:
A horizontal bracket over a group
of notes, usually indicating an ancient ligature if transcribed
into modern notation.  See also KievanLigature,
MensuralLigature, and VaticanaLigature.

grobs.name: LyricExtender
grobs.doc: An extender line in lyrics.

grobs.name: LyricHyphen
grobs.doc:
A hyphen in lyrics.  See also
VowelTransition.

grobs.name: LyricRepeatCount
grobs.doc: A repeat count in lyrics.

grobs.name: LyricSpace
grobs.doc: A space in lyrics.

grobs.name: LyricText
grobs.doc:
A chunk of text in lyrics.  See
also LyricExtender, LyricHyphen, LyricSpace,
and VowelTransition.

grobs.name: MeasureCounter
grobs.doc:
A grob to print a counter for
measures.

grobs.name: MeasureGrouping
grobs.doc:
A measure grouping or conducting
sign.

grobs.name: MeasureSpanner
grobs.doc:
A horizontal bracket between
bar lines.  See also HorizontalBracket.

grobs.name: MelodyItem
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob to help alter
the stem directions of middle notes on a staff so that they
follow the melody.

grobs.name: MensuralLigature
grobs.doc:
A grob to display a ligature as
used in mensural notation.  See also KievanLigature,
VaticanaLigature, and LigatureBracket.

grobs.name: MetronomeMark
grobs.doc:
A metronome mark.  This is
either a precise tempo indication like ‘quarter note = 80’, or
an arbitrary piece of text (like ‘Allegro’), possibly followed
by a precise indication in parentheses.

grobs.name: MultiMeasureRest
grobs.doc:
A multi-measure rest.  See also
MultiMeasureRestNumber, MultiMeasureRestText,
MultiMeasureRestScript, and Rest.

grobs.name: MultiMeasureRestNumber
grobs.doc:
A grob to print the length of a
MultiMeasureRest grob.

grobs.name: MultiMeasureRestScript
grobs.doc:
An articulation (like a fermata)
attached to a MultiMeasureRest grob.  See also
Script.

grobs.name: MultiMeasureRestText
grobs.doc:
A text markup for a
MultiMeasureRest grob.  See also TextScript.

grobs.name: NonMusicalPaperColumn
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob grouping
non-musical items to handle the flexible horizontal space between
non-musical and musical columns.  Grobs that have the property
`non-musical` set to `#t` belong to this column.

grobs.name: NoteCollision
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob to group
NoteColumn grobs from several voices, mainly to handle
note collisions.  See also RestCollision.

grobs.name: NoteColumn
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob to align
stacked notes, stems, flags, accidentals, and other items from
the same voice.  See also NoteCollision.

grobs.name: NoteHead
grobs.doc:
A note head.  See also
TabNoteHead.

grobs.name: NoteName
grobs.doc:
A textual representation of a
note name.

grobs.name: NoteSpacing
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob to handle
(horizontal) spacing of notes.  See also
GraceSpacing, StaffSpacing, and
SpacingSpanner.

grobs.name: OptionalMaterialBracket
grobs.doc:
An in-staff bracket delimiting an optional
passage.

grobs.name: OttavaBracket
grobs.doc: An ottava bracket.

grobs.name: PaperColumn
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob grouping
musical items to handle the flexible horizontal space between
musical and non-musical columns.  See also
NonMusicalPaperColumn.

grobs.name: Parentheses
grobs.doc:
A grob to create parentheses
around other grobs.

grobs.name: PercentRepeat
grobs.doc:
A percent symbol for repeating
a bar.  See also PercentRepeatCounter,
DoublePercentRepeat, DoubleRepeatSlash, and
RepeatSlash.

grobs.name: PercentRepeatCounter
grobs.doc:
A grob to print a counter for
PercentRepeat grobs.

grobs.name: PhrasingSlur
grobs.doc:
A phrasing slur, indicating a
‘musical sentence’.  See also Slur.

grobs.name: PianoPedalBracket
grobs.doc:
A piano pedal bracket.  It can
also be part of SostenutoPedal, SustainPedal, or
UnaCordaPedal grobs if they are printed in a bracketed
style.

grobs.name: RehearsalMark
grobs.doc: A rehearsal mark.

grobs.name: RepeatSlash
grobs.doc:
A symbol consisting of one or
more slashes for repeating patterns shorter than a single
measure, and which contain identical durations.  See also
PercentRepeat, DoublePercentRepeat, and
DoubleRepeatSlash.

grobs.name: RepeatTie
grobs.doc:
A repeat tie (i.e., a tie from
nothing to a note).  See also RepeatTieColumn,
LaissezVibrerTie, and Tie.

grobs.name: RepeatTieColumn
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob to determine
direction and shape of stacked RepeatTie grobs.

grobs.name: Rest
grobs.doc:
An ordinary rest.  See also
MultiMeasureRest.

grobs.name: RestCollision
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob to handle rest
collisions of different voices.  See also
NoteCollision.

grobs.name: Script
grobs.doc:
An articulation (staccato,
accent, etc.).  See also ScriptColumn,
ScriptRow, and MultiMeasureRestScript.

grobs.name: ScriptColumn
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob to
(vertically) align stacked Script grobs.

grobs.name: ScriptRow
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob to
horizontally align stacked Script grobs.

grobs.name: SectionLabel
grobs.doc:
A section label, for example
‘Coda’.

grobs.name: SegnoMark
grobs.doc:
A segno mark (created with
`\repeat segno`, not with `\segno`).

grobs.name: SignumRepetitionis
grobs.doc: An ancient end-repeat sign.

grobs.name: Slur
grobs.doc:
A slur.  See also
PhrasingSlur.

grobs.name: SostenutoPedal
grobs.doc:
A sostenuto pedal mark.  See
also SostenutoPedalLineSpanner, PianoPedalBracket,
SustainPedal, and UnaCordaPedal.

grobs.name: SostenutoPedalLineSpanner
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob providing a
baseline to align consecutive SostenutoPedal grobs
vertically.

grobs.name: SpacingSpanner
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob to set all
horizontal spacing constraints across a score.  There is normally
one such grob for the whole score, but there can be several if
`\newSpacingSection` is used.  See also
GraceSpacing, NoteSpacing, and
StaffSpacing.

grobs.name: SpanBar
grobs.doc:
A span bar, i.e., the parts of
a multi-staff bar line that are outside of staves.  See also
SpanBarStub.

grobs.name: SpanBarStub
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob, acting like a
fake SpanBar grob in contexts such as Lyrics that
are crossed by a span bar, to keep span bars taking horizontal
space.

grobs.name: StaffEllipsis
grobs.doc:
A visual marker (usually three
consecutive dots) to indicate that typesetting of music is
skipped.

grobs.name: StaffGrouper
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob to manage
vertical spacing of staff groups.  See also
VerticalAlignment and VerticalAxisGroup.

grobs.name: StaffHighlight
grobs.doc:
A colored span to highlight a music
passage.

grobs.name: StaffSpacing
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob to handle
spacing within a staff.  See also NoteSpacing,
GraceSpacing, and SpacingSpanner.

grobs.name: StaffSymbol
grobs.doc:
A staff symbol, usually
five horizontal lines.

grobs.name: StanzaNumber
grobs.doc:
A stanza number (or markup) for
lyrics.

grobs.name: Stem
grobs.doc:
A stem.  See also
StemStub.

grobs.name: StemStub
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob that prevents
cross-staff Stem grobs from colliding with
articulations.

grobs.name: StemTremolo
grobs.doc: A stem tremolo.

grobs.name: StringNumber
grobs.doc:
A markup (by default a digit in
a circle) to name a string.

grobs.name: StrokeFinger
grobs.doc:
A markup (usually a lowercase
letter) to indicate right-hand fingering.  See also
Fingering.

grobs.name: SustainPedal
grobs.doc:
A sustain pedal mark.  See also
SustainPedalLineSpanner, PianoPedalBracket,
SostenutoPedal, and UnaCordaPedal.

grobs.name: SustainPedalLineSpanner
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob providing a
baseline to align consecutive SustainPedal grobs
vertically.

grobs.name: System
grobs.doc:
The top-level grob of a score.
All other grobs are descendants of it.

grobs.name: SystemStartBar
grobs.doc:
A bar line as a system start
delimiter.

grobs.name: SystemStartBrace
grobs.doc:
A brace as a system start
delimiter.

grobs.name: SystemStartBracket
grobs.doc:
A bracket as a system start
delimiter.

grobs.name: SystemStartSquare
grobs.doc:
A rectangle-like bracket as a
start delimiter.

grobs.name: TabNoteHead
grobs.doc:
A ‘note head’ (usually a
digit) in a tablature.  See also NoteHead.

grobs.name: TextMark
grobs.doc:
An arbitrary textual mark.
See also SectionLabel and JumpScript for grobs with a
more specific intent.

grobs.name: TextScript
grobs.doc:
A markup attached to a grob like
a note head.  See also MultiMeasureRestText.

grobs.name: TextSpanner
grobs.doc:
Text like ‘rit’, usually
followed by a (dashed) line.  See also
DynamicTextSpanner.

grobs.name: Tie
grobs.doc:
A tie.  See also
TieColumn, LaissezVibrerTie, and
RepeatTie.

grobs.name: TieColumn
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob to determine
direction and shape of stacked Tie grobs.

grobs.name: TimeSignature
grobs.doc: A time signature.

grobs.name: TrillPitchAccidental
grobs.doc:
The accidental of a pitched
trill.  See also TrillPitchGroup.

grobs.name: TrillPitchGroup
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob to construct
a pitched trill, aligning TrillPitchAccidental,
TrillPitchParentheses, and TrillPitchHead
horizontally.  See also TrillSpanner.

grobs.name: TrillPitchHead
grobs.doc:
The note head of a pitched
trill.  See also TrillPitchGroup.

grobs.name: TrillPitchParentheses
grobs.doc:
The parentheses of a pitched
trill.  See also TrillPitchGroup.

grobs.name: TrillSpanner
grobs.doc:
A continued trill with a wiggly
line (created with `\startTrillSpan`, not with
`\trill`).  See also TrillPitchGroup.

grobs.name: TupletBracket
grobs.doc:
A tuplet bracket.  See also
TupletNumber.

grobs.name: TupletNumber
grobs.doc:
A tuplet number.  See also
TupletBracket.

grobs.name: UnaCordaPedal
grobs.doc:
An una corda pedal mark.  See
also UnaCordaPedalLineSpanner, SostenutoPedal,
SustainPedal, and PianoPedalBracket.

grobs.name: UnaCordaPedalLineSpanner
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob providing a
baseline to align consecutive UnaCordaPedal grobs
vertically.

grobs.name: VaticanaLigature
grobs.doc:
A grob to display a melisma
(ligature) as used in Gregorian chant.  See also
KievanLigature, MensuralLigature, and
LigatureBracket.

grobs.name: VerticalAlignment
grobs.doc:
A top-level auxiliary grob to
stack groups (staves, lyrics lines, etc.).  See also
StaffGrouper and VerticalAxisGroup.

grobs.name: VerticalAxisGroup
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob to group
everything contained in a context like Staff,
Lyrics, Dynamics, etc.  See also StaffGrouper
and VerticalAlignment.

grobs.name: VoiceFollower
grobs.doc:
A line to indicate staff changes
of a voice.

grobs.name: VoltaBracket
grobs.doc:
A volta bracket.  See also
VoltaBracketSpanner.

grobs.name: VoltaBracketSpanner
grobs.doc:
An auxiliary grob providing a
baseline to align consecutive VoltaBracket grobs
vertically.

grobs.name: VowelTransition
grobs.doc:
A vowel transition in
lyrics.  See also LyricHyphen.

grobProperties.name: X-align-on-main-noteheads
grobProperties.doc:
If true, this grob will
ignore suspended note heads when aligning itself on NoteColumn.

grobProperties.name: X-alignment-extent
grobProperties.doc:
If a grob wants to align
itself on a `PaperColumn` grob that doesn't contain note heads,
use this horizontal extent as a placeholder.

grobProperties.name: X-attachment
grobProperties.doc:
Horizontal attachment of a line on a
frame, typically between -1 (left) and 1 (right).

grobProperties.name: X-extent
grobProperties.doc:
Extent (size) in the X direction,
measured in staff-space units, relative to object's reference point.

grobProperties.name: X-offset
grobProperties.doc:
The horizontal amount that this object is
moved relative to its X-parent.

Note that many objects have special positioning considerations, which cause any
setting of `X-offset` to be ignored or modified, even though the object
supports the self-alignment-interface.

grobProperties.name: X-padding
grobProperties.doc:
Add this much extra space between objects that
are next to each other horizontally, overriding the `padding` property
value.

grobProperties.name: X-positions
grobProperties.doc:
Pair of X staff coordinates of a spanner
in the form `(*left* . *right*)`, where both *left* and
*right* are in `staff-space` units of the current staff.

grobProperties.name: Y-attachment
grobProperties.doc:
Vertical attachment of a line on a
frame, typically between -1 (down) and 1 (up).

grobProperties.name: Y-extent
grobProperties.doc:
Extent (size) in the Y direction,
measured in staff-space units, relative to object's reference point.

grobProperties.name: Y-offset
grobProperties.doc:
The vertical amount that this object is moved
relative to its Y-parent.

Note that many objects have special positioning considerations, which cause any
setting of `Y-offset` to be ignored or modified, even though the object
supports the self-alignment-interface.

grobProperties.name: accidental-padding
grobProperties.doc:
Property used by Beam to avoid
accidentals in whole-note tremolos.

grobProperties.name: add-stem-support
grobProperties.doc:
If set, the `Stem` object is
included in this script's support.

grobProperties.name: after-line-breaking
grobProperties.doc:
Dummy property, used to trigger
callback for `after-line-breaking`.

grobProperties.name: align-dir
grobProperties.doc:
Which side to align? `-1`: left side,
`0`: around center of width, `1`: right side.

grobProperties.name: allow-loose-spacing
grobProperties.doc:
If set, column can be detached
from main spacing.

grobProperties.name: allow-span-bar
grobProperties.doc:
If false, no inter-staff bar line will
be created below this bar line.

grobProperties.name: alteration
grobProperties.doc: Alteration numbers for accidental.

grobProperties.name: alteration-alist
grobProperties.doc:
List of `(*pitch*
. *accidental*)` pairs for key signature.

grobProperties.name: alteration-glyph-name-alist
grobProperties.doc: An alist of key-string pairs.

grobProperties.name: annotation-balloon
grobProperties.doc: Print the balloon around an annotation.

grobProperties.name: annotation-line
grobProperties.doc:
Print the line from an annotation to the
grob that it annotates.

grobProperties.name: arpeggio-direction
grobProperties.doc:
If set, put an arrow on the
arpeggio squiggly line.

grobProperties.name: arrow-length
grobProperties.doc: Arrow length.

grobProperties.name: arrow-width
grobProperties.doc: Arrow width.

grobProperties.name: auto-knee-gap
grobProperties.doc:
If a gap is found between note
heads where a horizontal beam fits and it is larger than this number,
make a kneed beam.

grobProperties.name: automatically-numbered
grobProperties.doc:
If set, footnotes are
automatically numbered.

grobProperties.name: average-spacing-wishes
grobProperties.doc:
If set, the spacing wishes are
averaged over staves.

grobProperties.name: avoid-note-head
grobProperties.doc:
If set, the stem of a chord does not
pass through all note heads, but starts at the last note head.

grobProperties.name: avoid-scripts
grobProperties.doc:
If set, a tuplet bracket avoids the
scripts associated with the note heads it encompasses.

grobProperties.name: avoid-slur
grobProperties.doc:
Method of handling slur collisions.
Choices are `inside`, `outside`, `around`, and
`ignore`.  `inside` adjusts the slur if needed to keep the
grob inside the slur.  `outside` moves the grob vertically to the
outside of the slur.  `around` moves the grob vertically to the
outside of the slur only if there is a collision.  `ignore` does
not move either.  In grobs whose notational significance depends on
vertical position (such as accidentals, clefs, etc.), `outside`
and `around` behave like `ignore`.

grobProperties.name: axes
grobProperties.doc:
List of axis numbers.  In the case of alignment
grobs, this should contain only one number.

grobProperties.name: bar-extent
grobProperties.doc:
The Y-extent of the actual bar line.
This may differ from `Y-extent` because it does not include the
dots in a repeat bar line.

grobProperties.name: base-shortest-duration
grobProperties.doc:
Spacing is based on the
shortest notes in a piece.  Normally, pieces are spaced as if notes at
least as short as this are present.

grobProperties.name: baseline-skip
grobProperties.doc:
Distance between base lines of
multiple lines of text.

grobProperties.name: beam-thickness
grobProperties.doc:
Beam thickness, measured in
`staff-space` units.

grobProperties.name: beam-width
grobProperties.doc: Width of the tremolo sign.

grobProperties.name: beamed-stem-shorten
grobProperties.doc:
How much to shorten beamed stems,
when their direction is forced.  It is a list, since the value is
different depending on the number of flags and beams.

grobProperties.name: beaming
grobProperties.doc:
Pair of number lists.  Each number list
specifies which beams to make.  `0` is the central beam,
`1` is the next beam toward the note, etc.  This information
is used to determine how to connect the beaming patterns from stem to
stem inside a beam.

grobProperties.name: beamlet-default-length
grobProperties.doc:
A pair of numbers.  The first
number specifies the default length of a beamlet that sticks out of
the left hand side of this stem; the second number specifies the
default length of the beamlet to the right.  The actual length of a
beamlet is determined by taking either the default length or the
length specified by `beamlet-max-length-proportion`, whichever is
smaller.

grobProperties.name: beamlet-max-length-proportion
grobProperties.doc:
The maximum length of a
beamlet, as a proportion of the distance between two adjacent stems.

grobProperties.name: before-line-breaking
grobProperties.doc:
Dummy property, used to trigger
a callback function.

grobProperties.name: bend-me
grobProperties.doc: Decide whether this grob is bent.

grobProperties.name: between-cols
grobProperties.doc: Where to attach a loose column to.

grobProperties.name: bound-details
grobProperties.doc:
An alist of properties for
determining attachments of spanners to edges.

grobProperties.name: bound-padding
grobProperties.doc:
The amount of padding to insert around
spanner bounds.

grobProperties.name: bound-prefatory-paddings
grobProperties.doc:
For a highlight,
the amount of padding to insert at a bound from a prefatory
item that is not a bar line.

grobProperties.name: bracket-flare
grobProperties.doc:
A pair of numbers specifying how
much edges of brackets should slant outward.  Value `0.0` means
straight edges.

grobProperties.name: bracket-visibility
grobProperties.doc:
This controls the
visibility of the tuplet bracket.  Setting it to `#f` prevents
printing of the bracket.  Setting the property to `if-no-beam`
makes it print only if there is no beam associated with this tuplet
bracket.

grobProperties.name: break-align-anchor
grobProperties.doc:
Grobs aligned to this breakable
item will have their X-offsets shifted by this number.  In bar lines,
for example, this is used to position grobs relative to the (visual)
center of the bar line.

grobProperties.name: break-align-anchor-alignment
grobProperties.doc:
Read by
`ly:break-aligned-interface::calc-extent-aligned-anchor` for
aligning an anchor to a grob's extent.

grobProperties.name: break-align-orders
grobProperties.doc:
This is a vector of 3 lists:
`#(*end-of-line* *unbroken* *start-of-line*`).
Each list contains *break-align symbols* that specify an
order of breakable items (see Grobs and their break-align symbols
and break-alignment-interface).

For example, this places time signatures before clefs:

```
\override Score.BreakAlignment.break-align-orders =
  #(make-vector 3 '(left-edge
                    cue-end-clef
                    ambitus
                    breathing-sign
                    time-signature
                    clef
                    cue-clef
                    staff-bar
                    key-cancellation
                    key-signature
                    custos))
```

The same result can be achieved more conveniently by:

```
\breakAlignInsert time-signature before clef
```

grobProperties.name: break-align-symbol
grobProperties.doc:
This key is used for aligning,
ordering, and spacing breakable items.  See
break-alignment-interface.

grobProperties.name: break-align-symbols
grobProperties.doc:
A list of
*break-align symbols* that determines which breakable
items to align this to.  If the grob selected by the first symbol
in the list is invisible due to `break-visibility`, we
will align to the next grob (and so on).  Choices are listed in
Grobs and their break-align symbols.

grobProperties.name: break-overshoot
grobProperties.doc:
A pair of numbers specifying how much a
broken spanner sticks out of its bounds horizontally on the broken side(s).  For
broken beams and broken tuplet brackets, the bounds are given by the prefatory
matter on the left and/or the rightmost column on the right.  For broken
horizontal brackets, the bounds are the leftmost and/or rightmost column; for
broken measure spanners, the left and/or right edge of the staff.

grobProperties.name: break-visibility
grobProperties.doc:
A vector of 3 booleans,
`#(*end-of-line* *unbroken* *begin-of-line*)`.
`#t` means visible, `#f` means killed.

grobProperties.name: break-visibility-passage-default
grobProperties.doc:
The value to use for
`break-@/visibility` when the item does not specifically mark the start or
end of a passage.  (It might be both or neither, depending on the type of
item.)

grobProperties.name: break-visibility-passage-end
grobProperties.doc:
The value to use for
`break-@/visibility` when the item marks the end of a passage.

grobProperties.name: break-visibility-passage-start
grobProperties.doc:
The value to use for
`break-@/visibility` when the item marks the start of a passage.

grobProperties.name: breakable
grobProperties.doc: Allow breaks here.

grobProperties.name: broken-bound-padding
grobProperties.doc:
The amount of padding to insert
when a spanner is broken at a line break.

grobProperties.name: chord-dots-limit
grobProperties.doc:
Limits the column of dots
on each chord to the height of the chord plus
`chord-dots-limit` staff positions.

grobProperties.name: circled-tip
grobProperties.doc:
Put a circle at start/@/end of
hairpins (al/@/del niente).

grobProperties.name: clef-alignments
grobProperties.doc:
An alist of parent-alignments
that should be used for clef modifiers with various clefs

grobProperties.name: clip-edges
grobProperties.doc:
Allow outward pointing beamlets at the
edges of beams?

grobProperties.name: collapse-height
grobProperties.doc:
Minimum height of system start
delimiter.  If equal or smaller, the bracket/@/brace/@/line is removed.

grobProperties.name: collision-interfaces
grobProperties.doc:
A list of interfaces for which
automatic beam-collision resolution is run.

grobProperties.name: collision-voice-only
grobProperties.doc:
Avoid beam collisions only with
grobs of the voice in which the beam was created.

grobProperties.name: color
grobProperties.doc: The color of this grob.

grobProperties.name: common-shortest-duration
grobProperties.doc:
The most common shortest
note length.  This is used in spacing.  Enlarging this sets the score
tighter.

grobProperties.name: concaveness
grobProperties.doc:
A beam is concave if its inner stems are
closer to the beam than the two outside stems.  This number is a
measure of the closeness of the inner stems.  It is used for damping
the slope of the beam.

grobProperties.name: connect-to-neighbor
grobProperties.doc:
Pair of booleans, indicating whether
this grob looks as a continued break.

grobProperties.name: control-points
grobProperties.doc:
List of offsets (number pairs) that form
control points for the tie, slur, or bracket shape.  For B@'eziers,
this should list the control points of a third-order B@'ezier curve.

grobProperties.name: count-from
grobProperties.doc:
The first measure in a measure count
receives this number.  The following measures are numbered in
increments from this initial value.

grobProperties.name: damping
grobProperties.doc: Amount of beam slope damping.

grobProperties.name: dash-definition
grobProperties.doc:
List of `dash-elements` defining the
dash structure.  Each `dash-element` has a starting t value,
an ending t-value, a `dash-fraction`, and a `dash-period`.

grobProperties.name: dash-fraction
grobProperties.doc:
Size of the dashes, relative to
`dash-period`.  Should be between `0.1` and
`1.0` (continuous line).  If set to `0.0`, a dotted line is
produced

grobProperties.name: dash-period
grobProperties.doc:
The length of one dash together with
whitespace.  If negative, no line is drawn at all.

grobProperties.name: dashed-edge
grobProperties.doc:
If set, the bracket edges are dashed like
the rest of the bracket.

grobProperties.name: default-direction
grobProperties.doc:
Direction determined by note head
positions.

grobProperties.name: default-staff-staff-spacing
grobProperties.doc:
The settings to use for
`staff-staff-spacing` when it is unset, for ungrouped staves
and for grouped staves that do not have the relevant
`StaffGrouper` property set (`staff-staff-spacing` or
`staffgroup-staff-spacing`).

grobProperties.name: denominator-style
grobProperties.doc:
The style of denominators in a time
signature.

grobProperties.name: details
grobProperties.doc:
An alist of parameters for detailed
grob behavior.  All layout objects for more information on the
available parameters and their default values of a particular grob's
`details` property.  Graphical Object Interfaces for
documentation of the available parameters.  Supporting interfaces can
be found at the bottom of a grob's description section.

grobProperties.name: digit-names
grobProperties.doc: Names for string finger digits.

grobProperties.name: direction
grobProperties.doc:
If `side-axis` is `0` (or
`X`), then this property determines whether the object is placed
`LEFT`, `CENTER` or `RIGHT` with respect to the
other object.  Otherwise, it determines whether the object is placed
`UP`, `CENTER` or `DOWN`.  Numerical values may also
be used: `UP`=`1`, `DOWN`=`-1`,
`LEFT`=`-1`, `RIGHT`=`1`,
`CENTER`=`0`.

grobProperties.name: dot-count
grobProperties.doc: The number of dots.

grobProperties.name: dot-negative-kern
grobProperties.doc:
The space to remove between a dot
and a slash in percent repeat glyphs.  Larger values bring the two
elements closer together.

grobProperties.name: dot-placement-list
grobProperties.doc:
List consisting of
`(*description* *string-number* *fret-number*
*finger-number*)` entries used to define fret diagrams.

grobProperties.name: double-stem-separation
grobProperties.doc:
The distance between the two
stems of a half note in tablature when using `\tabFullNotation`,
not counting the width of the stems themselves, expressed as a multiple
of the default height of a staff-space in the traditional five-line
staff.

grobProperties.name: duration-log
grobProperties.doc:
The 2-log of the note head duration,
i.e., `0` = whole note, `1` = half note, etc.

grobProperties.name: eccentricity
grobProperties.doc:
How asymmetrical to make a slur.
Positive means move the center to the right.

grobProperties.name: edge-height
grobProperties.doc:
A pair of numbers specifying the heights of
the vertical edges: `(*left-height* . *right-height*)`.

grobProperties.name: edge-text
grobProperties.doc:
A pair specifying the texts to be set at the
edges: `(*left-text* . *right-text*)`.

grobProperties.name: endpoint-alignments
grobProperties.doc:
A pair of numbers representing
the alignments of an object's endpoints.  E.g., the ends of a hairpin
relative to `NoteColumn` grobs.

grobProperties.name: expand-limit
grobProperties.doc:
Maximum number of measures expanded in
church rests.

grobProperties.name: extra-dy
grobProperties.doc: Slope glissandi this much extra.

grobProperties.name: extra-offset
grobProperties.doc:
A pair representing an offset.  This
offset is added just before outputting the symbol, so the typesetting
engine is completely oblivious to it.  The values are measured in
`staff-space` units of the staff's `StaffSymbol`.

grobProperties.name: extra-spacing-height
grobProperties.doc:
In the horizontal spacing
problem, we increase the height of each item by this amount (by adding
the ‘car’ to the bottom of the item and adding the ‘cdr’ to the
top of the item).  In order to make a grob infinitely high (to prevent
the horizontal spacing problem from placing any other grobs above or
below this grob), set this to `(-inf.0 . +inf.0)`.

grobProperties.name: extra-spacing-width
grobProperties.doc:
In the horizontal spacing
problem, we pad each item by this amount (by adding the ‘car’ on the
left side of the item and adding the ‘cdr’ on the right side of the
item).  In order to make a grob take up no horizontal space at all,
set this to `(+inf.0 . -inf.0)`.

grobProperties.name: extroversion
grobProperties.doc:
For polygons, how the thickness of the
line is spread on each side of the exact polygon with ideal zero
thickness.  If this is 0, the middle of line is on the polygon.
If 1, the line sticks out of the polygon.  If -1, the outer
side of the line is exactly on the polygon.  Other numeric values
are interpolated.

grobProperties.name: fa-merge-direction
grobProperties.doc:
If two ‘fa’ shape note heads get
merged that are both listed in the `fa-styles` property but
have different stem directions, enforce this note head direction
for display.

grobProperties.name: filled
grobProperties.doc: Whether an object is filled with ink.

grobProperties.name: flag-count
grobProperties.doc: The number of tremolo beams.

grobProperties.name: flag-style
grobProperties.doc:
The style of flags to be displayed within
markups (via `\note-by-number`).  Available are
`'modern-straight-flag`, `'old-straight-flag`,
`'flat-flag`, `'mensural`, `'stacked`,
and `'default`.

grobProperties.name: flat-positions
grobProperties.doc:
Flats in key signatures are placed
within the specified ranges of staff positions.  The general form
is a list of pairs, with one pair for each type of clef, in order
of the staff position at which each clef places C:
`(alto treble tenor soprano baritone mezzosoprano bass)`.
If the list contains a single element it applies for all clefs.
A single number in place of a pair sets accidentals within the octave
ending at that staff position.

grobProperties.name: font-encoding
grobProperties.doc:
The font encoding is the broadest
category for selecting a font.  Currently, only LilyPond's system
fonts (Emmentaler) are using this property.  Available
values are `fetaMusic` (Emmentaler), `fetaBraces`,
`fetaText` (Emmentaler).

grobProperties.name: font-family
grobProperties.doc:
The font family is the broadest category
for selecting text fonts.  Options include `serif`, `sans`
and `typewriter`.

grobProperties.name: font-features
grobProperties.doc: Opentype features.

grobProperties.name: font-name
grobProperties.doc:
This property is kept for backwards compatibility
only.  Use the `fonts` property instead.

grobProperties.name: font-series
grobProperties.doc:
Select the series of a font.  Common
choices are `normal` and `bold`.  The full list of symbols
that can be used is: `thin`, `ultralight` (or
`extralight`), `light`, `semilight` (or
`demilight`), `book`, `normal` (or `regular`),
`medium`, `semibold` (or `demibold`), `bold`,
`ultrabold` (or `extrabold`), `heavy` (or `black`),
and `ultraheavy` (or `ultrablack` or `extrablack`).

grobProperties.name: font-shape
grobProperties.doc:
Select the shape of a font.  Possible values
are `upright`, `italic`, `oblique`, and `slanted`
(which is the same as `oblique`).

grobProperties.name: font-size
grobProperties.doc:
The font size, compared to the
‘normal’ size.  `0` is style-sheet's normal size,
`-1` is smaller, `+1` is bigger.  Each step of 1 is
approximately 12% larger; 6 steps are exactly a factor 2
larger.  If the context property `fontSize` is set, its value is
added to this before the glyph is printed.  Fractional values are
allowed.

grobProperties.name: font-stretch
grobProperties.doc:
Select a condensed or expanded
font, if available in the font family.  Possible values are
`ultra-condensed`, `extra-condensed`, `condensed`,
`semi-condensed`, `normal`, `semi-expanded`, `expanded`,
`extra-expanded`, and `ultra-expanded`.

grobProperties.name: font-variant
grobProperties.doc:
Select the variant of a font.
Choices include `normal` and `small-caps`.

grobProperties.name: fonts
grobProperties.doc:
An alist mapping font families to
font names.  The standard font families are `music`, `serif`,
`sans` and `typewriter`.

grobProperties.name: footnote
grobProperties.doc: Should this be a footnote or in-note?

grobProperties.name: footnote-music
grobProperties.doc: Music creating a footnote.

grobProperties.name: footnote-text
grobProperties.doc: A footnote for the grob.

grobProperties.name: force-hshift
grobProperties.doc:
This specifies a manual shift for notes
in collisions.  The unit is the note head width of the first down-stem
voice note; if there are no down-stem voices, the width of the first
up-stem voice note is taken instead.  This is used by
note-collision-interface.

grobProperties.name: forced-spacing
grobProperties.doc:
Spacing forced between grobs, used in
various ligature engravers.

grobProperties.name: fraction
grobProperties.doc: A fraction.

grobProperties.name: french-beaming
grobProperties.doc:
Use French beaming style for this
stem.  The stem stops at the innermost beams.

grobProperties.name: fret-diagram-details
grobProperties.doc:
An alist of detailed grob
properties for fret diagrams.  Each alist entry consists of a
`(*property* .  *value*)` pair.  The properties which can
be included in `fret-diagram-details` include the following:

-
`barre-type` -- Type of barre indication used.  Choices include
`curved`, `straight`, and `none`.  Default
`curved`.

- `barre-thickness` -- Thickness of barre line, in multiples of
`dot-radius`.  Only defined for `barre-type=straight`.  Default
value 1.

-
`capo-thickness` -- Thickness of capo indicator, in multiples of
fret-space.  Default value 0.5.
-
`dot-color` -- Color of dots.  Options include `black` and
`white`.  Default `black`.
-
`dot-label-font-mag` -- Magnification for font used to label fret
dots.  Default value 1.
-
`dot-position` -- Location of dot in fret space.  Default 0.6 for
dots without labels, 0.95-`dot-radius` for dots with labels.
-
`dot-radius` -- Radius of dots, in terms of fret spaces.  Default
value 0.425 for labeled dots, 0.25 for unlabeled dots.
-
`finger-code` -- Code for the type of fingering indication used.
Options include `none`, `in-dot`, and `below-string`.
Default `none` for markup fret diagrams, `below-string` for
`FretBoards` fret diagrams.
-
`fret-count` -- The number of frets.  Default 4.
-
`fret-distance` -- Multiplier to adjust the distance between frets.
Default 1.0.
-
`fret-label-custom-format` -- The format string to be used label
the lowest fret number, when `number-type` equals to
`custom`.  Default "~a".
-
`fret-label-font-mag` -- The magnification of the font used to
label the lowest fret number.  Default 0.5.
-
`fret-label-vertical-offset` -- The offset of the fret label from
the center of the fret in direction parallel to strings.
Default 0.
-
`fret-label-horizontal-offset` -- The offset of the fret label from
the center of the fret in direction orthogonal to strings.
Default 0.
-
`handedness` -- Print the fret-diagram left- or right-handed.
`-1`, `LEFT` for left ; `1`, `RIGHT` for right.
Default `RIGHT`.
-
`paren-padding` -- The padding for the parenthesis.
Default 0.05.
-
`label-dir` -- Side to which the fret label is attached.
`-1`, `LEFT`, or `DOWN` for left or down; `1`,
`RIGHT`, or `UP` for right or up.  Default `RIGHT`.
-
`mute-string` -- Character string to be used to indicate muted
string.  Default `"x"`.
-
`number-type` -- Type of numbers to use in fret label.  Choices
include `arabic`, `roman-ij-lower`, `roman-ij-upper`,
`roman-lower`, `roman-upper`, `arabic` and
`custom`.  In the last case, the format string is supplied by the
`fret-label-custom-format` property.
Default `roman-lower`.
-
`open-string` -- Character string to be used to indicate open
string.  Default `"o"`.
-
`orientation` -- Orientation of fret-diagram.  Options include
`normal`, `landscape`, and `opposing-landscape`.
Default `normal`.
-
`string-count` -- The number of strings.  Default 6.
-
`string-distance` -- Multiplier to adjust the distance between strings.
Default 1.0.
-
`string-label-font-mag` -- The magnification of the font used to
label fingerings at the string, rather than in the dot.  Default value
0.6 for `normal` orientation, 0.5 for `landscape` and
`opposing-landscape`.
-
`string-overhang` -- Extension of string lines beyond last fret line,
in multiples of `fret-distance`.  Default value 1.
-
`string-thickness-factor` -- Factor for changing thickness of
each string in the fret diagram.  Thickness of string *k* is given
by `thickness`
* (1+`string-thickness-factor`) ^ (*k*-1).
Default 0.
-
`top-fret-thickness` -- The thickness of the top fret line, as a
multiple of the standard thickness.  Default value 3.
-
`xo-font-magnification` -- Magnification used for mute and open
string indicators.  Default value 0.5.
-
`xo-padding` -- Padding for open and mute indicators from top
fret.  Default value 0.25.

grobProperties.name: full-length-padding
grobProperties.doc:
How much padding to use at the
right side of a full-length tuplet bracket.

grobProperties.name: full-length-to-extent
grobProperties.doc:
Run to the extent of the column
for a full-length tuplet bracket.

grobProperties.name: full-measure-extra-space
grobProperties.doc:
Extra space that is allocated
at the beginning of a measure with only one note.  This property is
read from the NonMusicalPaperColumn that begins the measure.

grobProperties.name: full-size-change
grobProperties.doc: Don't make a change clef smaller.

grobProperties.name: gap
grobProperties.doc: Size of a gap in a variable symbol.

grobProperties.name: gap-count
grobProperties.doc:
Number of ‘floating’ beams in a two-stem
tremolo.

grobProperties.name: glissando-skip
grobProperties.doc:
Should this `NoteHead` be skipped
by glissandi?

grobProperties.name: glyph
grobProperties.doc:
A string determining what ‘style’ of glyph is
typeset.  Valid choices depend on the function that is reading this
property.

In combination with (span) bar lines, it is a string resembling the
bar line appearance in ASCII form.

grobProperties.name: glyph-left
grobProperties.doc:
The `glyph` value to use at the end of
the line when the line is broken.  `#f` indicates that no glyph
should be visible; otherwise the value must be a string.

grobProperties.name: glyph-name
grobProperties.doc:
The glyph name within the font.

In the context of (span) bar lines or clefs, *glyph-name* represents
a processed form of `glyph`, where decisions about line breaking,
etc., are already taken.

grobProperties.name: glyph-right
grobProperties.doc:
The `glyph` value to use at the
beginning of the line when the line is broken.  `#f` indicates
that no glyph should be visible; otherwise the value must be a string.

grobProperties.name: graphical
grobProperties.doc: Display in graphical (vs. text) form.

grobProperties.name: grow-direction
grobProperties.doc: Crescendo or decrescendo?

grobProperties.name: hair-thickness
grobProperties.doc:
Thickness of the thin line in a bar
line, expressed as a multiple of the default staff-line
thickness (i.e., the visual output is *not* influenced by changes
to `*Staff*.StaffSymbol.thickness`).

grobProperties.name: harp-pedal-details
grobProperties.doc:
An alist of detailed grob
properties for harp pedal diagrams.  Each alist entry consists of a
`(*property* . *value*)` pair.  The properties which can
be included in harp-pedal-details include the following:

-
`box-offset` -- Vertical shift of the center of flat/@/sharp pedal
boxes above/@/below the horizontal line.  Default value 0.8.
-
`box-width` -- Width of each pedal box.  Default value 0.4.
-
`box-height` -- Height of each pedal box.  Default value 1.0.
-
`space-before-divider` -- Space between boxes before the first
divider (so that the diagram can be made symmetric).  Default
value 0.8.
-
`space-after-divider` -- Space between boxes after the first
divider.  Default value 0.8.
-
`circle-thickness` -- Thickness (in unit of the line-thickness)
of the ellipse around circled pedals.  Default value 0.5.
-
`circle-x-padding` -- Padding in X direction of the ellipse
around circled pedals.  Default value 0.15.
-
`circle-y-padding` -- Padding in Y direction of the ellipse
around circled pedals.  Default value 0.2.

grobProperties.name: head-direction
grobProperties.doc:
Are the note heads left or right in a
semitie?

grobProperties.name: height
grobProperties.doc:
Height of an object in `staff-space`
units.

grobProperties.name: height-limit
grobProperties.doc:
Maximum slur height: The longer the
slur, the closer it is to this height.

grobProperties.name: hide-tied-accidental-after-break
grobProperties.doc:
If set, an accidental
that appears on a tied note after a line break will not be displayed.

grobProperties.name: horizon-padding
grobProperties.doc:
The amount to pad the axis
along which a `Skyline` is built for the
`side-position-interface`.

grobProperties.name: horizontal-shift
grobProperties.doc:
An integer that identifies ranking
of `NoteColumn`s for horizontal shifting.  This is used by
note-collision-interface.

grobProperties.name: horizontal-skylines
grobProperties.doc:
Two skylines, one to the
left and one to the right of this grob.

grobProperties.name: id
grobProperties.doc: An id string for the grob.

grobProperties.name: ignore-ambitus
grobProperties.doc:
If set, don't consider this note head
for ambitus calculation.

grobProperties.name: ignore-collision
grobProperties.doc:
If set, don't do note collision
resolution on this `NoteColumn`.

grobProperties.name: implicit
grobProperties.doc: Is this an implicit bass figure?

grobProperties.name: inspect-quants
grobProperties.doc:
If debugging is set, set beam and
slur position to a (quantized) position that is as close as possible
to this value, and print the demerits for the inspected position in
the output.

grobProperties.name: keep-inside-line
grobProperties.doc:
If set, this column cannot have
objects sticking into the margin.

grobProperties.name: kern
grobProperties.doc:
The space between individual elements
in any compound bar line, expressed as a multiple of the default
staff-line thickness (i.e., the visual output is *not*
influenced by changes to
`*Staff*.StaffSymbol.thickness`).

grobProperties.name: knee
grobProperties.doc: Is this beam kneed?

grobProperties.name: knee-spacing-correction
grobProperties.doc:
Factor for the optical
correction amount for kneed beams.  Set between `0` for no
correction and `1` for full correction.

grobProperties.name: knee-to-beam
grobProperties.doc:
Determines whether a tuplet number
will be positioned next to a kneed beam.

grobProperties.name: labels
grobProperties.doc: List of labels (symbols) placed on a column.

grobProperties.name: layer
grobProperties.doc:
An integer which determines the order of printing
objects.  Objects with the lowest value of layer are drawn first, then
objects with progressively higher values are drawn, so objects with
higher values overwrite objects with lower values.  By default most
objects are assigned a layer value of 1.

grobProperties.name: ledger-extra
grobProperties.doc:
A distance relative to a note head's vertical
position to modify the range where ledger lines are drawn, depending on the
actually used ledger line positions.  If positive, this range gets extended,
possibly adding extra ledger lines.  If negative, the range gets reduced,
possibly removing ledger lines.

grobProperties.name: ledger-line-thickness
grobProperties.doc:
The thickness of ledger
lines.  It is the sum of two numbers: The first is the factor for line
thickness, and the second for staff space.  Both contributions are added.

grobProperties.name: ledger-positions
grobProperties.doc:
A list of vertical positions of ledger lines.
Its exact behavior depends on the grob; see StaffSymbol,
NoteHead, Custos, and Script.

grobProperties.name: ledger-positions-function
grobProperties.doc:
A quoted Scheme procedure that takes
a `StaffSymbol` grob and the vertical position of a note head as arguments
and returns a list of ledger line positions.

grobProperties.name: left-bound-info
grobProperties.doc:
An alist of properties for
determining attachments of spanners to edges.

grobProperties.name: left-number-text
grobProperties.doc:
For a measure counter, this is the
formatted measure count.  When the measure counter extends over several
measures (like with compressed multi-measure rests), it is the text
on the left side of the dash.

grobProperties.name: left-padding
grobProperties.doc:
The amount of space that is put
left to an object (e.g., a lyric extender).

grobProperties.name: length
grobProperties.doc:
User override for the stem length of
unbeamed stems (each unit represents half a `staff-space`).

grobProperties.name: length-fraction
grobProperties.doc:
Multiplier for lengths.  Used for
determining ledger lines and stem lengths.

grobProperties.name: line-break-penalty
grobProperties.doc:
Penalty for a line break at this
column.  This affects the choices of the line breaker; it avoids a
line break at a column with a positive penalty and prefers a line
break at a column with a negative penalty.

grobProperties.name: line-break-permission
grobProperties.doc:
Instructs the line breaker on
whether to put a line break at this column.  Can be `force` or
`allow`.

grobProperties.name: line-break-system-details
grobProperties.doc:
An alist of
subproperties to use if this column is the start of a system.

-
`alignment-distances` -- A list of vertical distances between
the staves of a system.
-
`bottom-padding` -- If set for the lowest staff of the
bottommost system on a page, it specifies the distance between the
bottom of the page and the lowest staff.
-
`extra-offset` -- A pair of horizontal and vertical offsets
for the current staff, relative to either the default layout
positions or the positions given with the `X-offset` and
`Y-offset` subproperties.
-
`X-offset` -- Horizontal (absolute) starting point of the
current staff.
-
`Y-offset` -- Vertical (absolute) starting point of the
current staff.

grobProperties.name: line-count
grobProperties.doc: The number of staff lines.

grobProperties.name: line-positions
grobProperties.doc: Vertical positions of staff lines.

grobProperties.name: line-thickness
grobProperties.doc:
For slurs and ties, this is the
diameter of the virtual “pen” that draws the two arcs of the
curve's outline, which intersect at the endpoints.  This property is
expressed as a multiple of the current staff-line thickness (i.e., the
visual output is influenced by changes to
`*Staff*.StaffSymbol.thickness`).

grobProperties.name: long-text
grobProperties.doc: Text markup.  See Formatting text.

grobProperties.name: main-extent
grobProperties.doc:
The horizontal extent of a
`NoteColumn` grob without taking suspended `NoteHead`
grobs into account (i.e., `NoteHead`s forced into the unnatural
direction of the `Stem` because of a chromatic clash).

grobProperties.name: max-beam-connect
grobProperties.doc:
Maximum number of beams to connect
to beams from this stem.  Further beams are typeset as beamlets.

grobProperties.name: max-slope-factor
grobProperties.doc:
Factor for calculating
the maximum tuplet bracket slope.  Notice that there exists a homonymous
property for slurs.

grobProperties.name: max-symbol-separation
grobProperties.doc:
The maximum distance between
symbols making up a church rest.

grobProperties.name: maximum-gap
grobProperties.doc:
Maximum value allowed for `gap`
property.

grobProperties.name: measure-count
grobProperties.doc:
The number of measures for a
multi-measure rest.

grobProperties.name: measure-division
grobProperties.doc:
A list representing what fraction
of the measure length each chord name takes in a chord square.  The list
is made of exact numbers between 0 and 1, which should add up to 1.
Example: a measure `c2 g4 g4` results in `'(1/2 1/4 1/4)`.

grobProperties.name: measure-division-chord-placement-alist
grobProperties.doc:
An alist mapping
measure divisions (see the `measure-division` property) to lists
of coordinates (number pairs) applied to the chord names of a chord
square.  Coordinates are normalized between -1 and 1 within the square.

grobProperties.name: measure-division-lines-alist
grobProperties.doc:
An alist mapping measure
