divisions (see the `measure-division` property) to lists of lines
to draw in the square, given as 4-element lists:
`(*x-start* *y-start* *x-end* *y-end*)`.

grobProperties.name: measure-length
grobProperties.type: positive moment with no grace part
grobProperties.doc:
Length of a measure.
Used in some spacing situations.

grobProperties.name: merge-differently-dotted
grobProperties.doc:
Merge note heads in
collisions, even if they have a different number of dots.  This is
normal notation for some types of polyphonic music.

`merge-differently-dotted` only applies to opposing stem
directions (i.e., voice 1 & 2).

grobProperties.name: merge-differently-headed
grobProperties.doc:
Merge note heads in
collisions, even if they have different note heads.  The smaller of
the two heads is rendered invisible.  This is used in polyphonic
guitar notation.  The value of this setting is used by
note-collision-interface.

`merge-differently-headed` only applies to opposing stem
directions (i.e., voice 1 & 2).

grobProperties.name: minimum-X-extent
grobProperties.doc:
Minimum size of an object in
X dimension, measured in `staff-space` units.

grobProperties.name: minimum-X-space
grobProperties.doc:
Minimum distance that the victim
should move horizontally (after padding), overriding the
`minimum-space` property value.

grobProperties.name: minimum-Y-extent
grobProperties.doc:
Minimum size of an object in
Y dimension, measured in `staff-space` units.

grobProperties.name: minimum-distance
grobProperties.doc:
Minimum distance between rest
and notes or beam.

grobProperties.name: minimum-length
grobProperties.doc:
Try to make a spanner at least
this long, normally in the horizontal direction.  This requires an
appropriate callback for the `springs-and-rods` property.  If
added to a `Tie`, this sets the minimum distance between
note heads.

grobProperties.name: minimum-length-after-break
grobProperties.doc:
If set, try to make
a broken spanner starting a line this long.  This requires an
appropriate callback for the `springs-and-rods` property.  If
added to a `Tie`, this sets the minimum distance to the
note head.

grobProperties.name: minimum-length-fraction
grobProperties.doc:
Minimum length of ledger line
as fraction of note head size.

grobProperties.name: minimum-space
grobProperties.doc:
Minimum distance that the victim
should move (after padding).

grobProperties.name: musical-length
grobProperties.type: non-negative moment with no grace part
grobProperties.doc: Musical length.

grobProperties.name: nested-fraction-mixed
grobProperties.doc:
Whether a fractional term of a time
signature is printed as a mixed number (e.g., ‘2 1/2’) or as a common
fraction (e.g., ‘5/2’).

grobProperties.name: nested-fraction-orientation
grobProperties.doc:
A symbol describing the orientation
of a fractional part of a time signature.

grobProperties.name: nested-fraction-relative-font-size
grobProperties.doc:
The font size of a numeral in
a fractional term of a time signature, relative to size of the whole numbers.

grobProperties.name: neutral-direction
grobProperties.doc:
Which direction to take in the
center of the staff.

grobProperties.name: neutral-position
grobProperties.doc:
Position (in half staff spaces) where
to flip the direction of custos stem.

grobProperties.name: next
grobProperties.doc:
Object that is next relation (e.g., the lyric
syllable following an extender).

grobProperties.name: no-ledgers
grobProperties.doc:
If set, don't draw ledger lines on this
object.

grobProperties.name: no-stem-extend
grobProperties.doc:
If set, notes with ledger lines do not
get stems extending to the middle staff line.

grobProperties.name: non-break-align-symbols
grobProperties.doc:
A list of symbols that determine
which NON-break-aligned interfaces to align this to.

grobProperties.name: non-default
grobProperties.doc: Set for manually specified clefs and keys.

grobProperties.name: non-musical
grobProperties.doc:
True if the grob belongs to a
`NonMusicalPaperColumn`.

grobProperties.name: nonstaff-nonstaff-spacing
grobProperties.doc:
The spacing alist
controlling the distance between the current non-staff line and
the next non-staff line in the direction of `staff-affinity`,
if both are on the same side of the related staff, and
`staff-affinity` is either `UP` or `DOWN`.  See
`staff-staff-spacing` for a description of the alist
structure.

grobProperties.name: nonstaff-relatedstaff-spacing
grobProperties.doc:
The spacing
alist controlling the distance between the current non-staff line and
the nearest staff in the direction of `staff-affinity`, if
there are no non-staff lines between the two, and
`staff-affinity` is either `UP` or `DOWN`.  If
`staff-affinity` is `CENTER`, then
`nonstaff-relatedstaff-spacing` is used for the nearest
staves on *both* sides, even if other non-staff lines appear
between the current one and either of the staves.  See
`staff-staff-spacing` for a description of the alist
structure.

grobProperties.name: nonstaff-unrelatedstaff-spacing
grobProperties.doc:
The spacing
alist controlling the distance between the current non-staff line and
the nearest staff in the opposite direction from
`staff-affinity`, if there are no other non-staff lines
between the two, and `staff-affinity` is either `UP` or
`DOWN`.  See `staff-staff-spacing` for a description of
the alist structure.

grobProperties.name: normalized-endpoints
grobProperties.doc:
Represents left and right placement
over the total spanner, where the width of the spanner is normalized
between 0 and 1.

grobProperties.name: note-collision-threshold
grobProperties.doc:
Simultaneous notes that
are this close or closer in units of `staff-space` will be
identified as vertically colliding. Used by `Stem` grobs for notes
in the same voice, and `NoteCollision` grobs for notes in
different voices. Default value 1.

grobProperties.name: note-dots-direction
grobProperties.doc:
Whether the augmentation dots are shifted up
or down (or not shifted) relative to the note head in a number-over-note time
signature.

grobProperties.name: note-flag-style
grobProperties.doc:
The style of the flags in a number-over-note
time signature.  See `flag-style`.

grobProperties.name: note-head-style
grobProperties.doc:
The style of the note head in a number-over-note
time signature.  See Note head styles.

grobProperties.name: note-names
grobProperties.doc:
Vector of strings containing names for
easy-notation note heads.

grobProperties.name: note-staff-position
grobProperties.doc:
The position of the note in a
number-over-note time signature.  See `staff-position`.

grobProperties.name: number-range-separator
grobProperties.doc:
For a measure counter extending over
several measures (like with compressed multi-measure rests), this is
the separator between the two printed numbers.

grobProperties.name: number-type
grobProperties.doc:
Numbering style.  Choices include
`arabic`, `roman-ij-lower`, `roman-ij-upper`,
`roman-lower`, and `roman-upper`.

grobProperties.name: output-attributes
grobProperties.doc:
An alist of attributes for the grob, to
be included in output files.  When the SVG typesetting backend is used,
the attributes are assigned to a group (`<g>`) containing all of the
stencils that comprise a given grob.  For example,

```
'((id . 123) (class . foo) (data-whatever . "bar"))
```

produces

```
<g id="123" class="foo" data-whatever="bar"> … </g>
```

In the PostScript backend, where there is no way to group items, the
setting of the `output-@/attributes` property has no effect.

grobProperties.name: outside-staff-horizontal-padding
grobProperties.doc:
By default, an
outside-staff-object can be placed so that is it very close to another
grob horizontally.  If this property is set, the outside-staff-object
is raised so that it is not so close to its neighbor.

grobProperties.name: outside-staff-padding
grobProperties.doc:
The padding to place between
grobs when spacing according to `outside-@/staff-@/priority`.
Two grobs with different `outside-@/staff-@/padding` values have
the larger value of padding between them.

grobProperties.name: outside-staff-placement-directive
grobProperties.doc:
One of four directives
telling how outside staff objects should be placed.

-
`left-to-right-greedy` -- Place each successive grob from left to
right.
-
`left-to-right-polite` -- Place a grob from left to right only if
it does not potentially overlap with another grob that has been placed
on a pass through a grob array. If there is overlap, do another pass to
determine placement.
-
`right-to-left-greedy` -- Same as `left-to-right-greedy`, but
from right to left.
-
`right-to-left-polite` -- Same as `left-to-right-polite`, but
from right to left.

grobProperties.name: outside-staff-priority
grobProperties.doc:
If set, the grob is positioned
outside the staff in such a way as to avoid all collisions.  In case
of a potential collision, the grob with the smaller
`outside-staff-priority` is closer to the staff.

grobProperties.name: packed-spacing
grobProperties.doc:
If set, the notes are spaced as
tightly as possible.

grobProperties.name: padding
grobProperties.doc:
Add this much extra space between
objects that are next to each other.

grobProperties.name: padding-pairs
grobProperties.doc:
An alist of padding pairs for key
signatures (and key cancellations).  Each alist entry has the form

```
((left-glyph-name . right-glyph-name) . dist)
```

specifying the padding *dist* between two adjacent key signature
elements.  If there is no entry in the alist for a given pair, the
padding value given by the `padding` property of the
`KeySignature` (or `KeyCancellation`) grob is used instead.

A special feature is the handling of adjacent naturals (to be more precise,
the handling of glyph `accidentals@/.natural`): If there is no
‘natural-natural’ entry in `padding-pairs` explicitly overriding it,
LilyPond adds some extra padding (in addition to the grob's `padding`
value) to avoid collisions.

grobProperties.name: page-break-penalty
grobProperties.doc:
Penalty for page break at this
column.  This affects the choices of the page breaker; it avoids a
page break at a column with a positive penalty and prefers a page
break at a column with a negative penalty.

grobProperties.name: page-break-permission
grobProperties.doc:
Instructs the page breaker on
whether to put a page break at this column.  Can be `force` or
`allow`.

grobProperties.name: page-number
grobProperties.doc: Page number on which this system ends up.

grobProperties.name: page-turn-penalty
grobProperties.doc:
Penalty for a page turn at this
column.  This affects the choices of the page breaker; it avoids a
page turn at a column with a positive penalty and prefers a page turn
at a column with a negative penalty.

grobProperties.name: page-turn-permission
grobProperties.doc:
Instructs the page breaker on
whether to put a page turn at this column.  Can be `force` or
`allow`.

grobProperties.name: parent-alignment-X
grobProperties.doc:
Specify on which point
of the parent the object is aligned. The value `-1` means
aligned on parent's left edge, `0` on center, and
`1` right edge, in X direction.  Other numerical
values may also be specified - the unit is half the parent's width.
If not a number, align on the parent's reference point.
If unset, the value from `self-alignment-X` property will be
used.

grobProperties.name: parent-alignment-Y
grobProperties.doc:
Like `parent-alignment-X`
but for the Y axis.

grobProperties.name: parenthesis-friends
grobProperties.doc:
A list of Grob types, as symbols.
When parentheses enclose a Grob that has 'parenthesis-friends, the
parentheses widen to include any child Grobs with type among
'parenthesis-friends.

grobProperties.name: parenthesis-id
grobProperties.doc:
When parenthesized grobs created in the
same time step have this property, there is one set of parentheses for
each group of grobs having the same value.

grobProperties.name: parenthesized
grobProperties.doc: Parenthesize this grob.

grobProperties.name: positions
grobProperties.doc:
Pair of staff coordinates
`(*start* . *end*)`, where *start* and
*end* are vertical positions in `staff-space` units of the current
staff.  For slurs, this value selects which slur candidate to use; if extreme
positions are requested, the closest one is taken.

grobProperties.name: prefer-dotted-right
grobProperties.doc:
For note collisions, prefer to
shift dotted up-note to the right, rather than shifting just the
dot.

grobProperties.name: protrusion
grobProperties.doc:
In a bracket indicating non-arpeggio or optional
material, the length of the horizontal edges.

grobProperties.name: range-collapse-threshold
grobProperties.doc:
If the length of a volta
range is greater than or equal to this threshold, print it with
a dash.  For example, if this is 3, a `\volta 1,2,3` is
printed as `1.-3.`, but if it is 4, it is printed as
`1.2.3.`.

grobProperties.name: rank-on-page
grobProperties.doc: 0-based index of the system on a page.

grobProperties.name: ratio
grobProperties.doc:
Parameter for slur shape.  The higher this
number, the quicker the slur attains its `height-limit`.

grobProperties.name: remove-empty
grobProperties.doc:
If set, remove group if it contains no
interesting items.

grobProperties.name: remove-first
grobProperties.doc:
Remove the first staff of an orchestral
score?

grobProperties.name: remove-layer
grobProperties.doc:
When set as a positive integer, the
`Keep_alive_together_engraver` removes all
`VerticalAxisGroup` grobs with a `remove-layer` larger than
the smallest retained `remove-layer`. Set to `#f` to make a
layer independent of the `Keep_alive_together_engraver`. Set to
`'()`, the layer does not participate in the layering decisions.
The property can also be set as a symbol for common behaviors:
`#'any` to keep the layer alive with any other layer in the
group; `#'above` or `#'below` to keep the layer alive with
the context immediately before or after it, respectively.

grobProperties.name: remove-short-autoextender
grobProperties.doc:
If set, auto-generated
unbroken lyric extenders are removed if the lyric syllable stretches
up to the last contained note head.

grobProperties.name: replacement-alist
grobProperties.doc:
Alist of strings.
The key is a string of the pattern to be replaced.  The value is a
string of what should be displayed.  Useful for ligatures.

grobProperties.name: restore-first
grobProperties.doc:
Print a natural before the
accidental.

grobProperties.name: rhythmic-location
grobProperties.doc:
Where (bar number,
measure position) in the score.

grobProperties.name: right-bound-info
grobProperties.doc:
An alist of properties for
determining attachments of spanners to edges.

grobProperties.name: right-justified
grobProperties.doc:
Used for `BarLine`s to right-align them.
Usually the extent of a `BarLine` has some positive value to the right.  If
this property is set to `#t`, `BarLine.stencil` is translated to the
left by this value.  Needs to be set at `Score` or `StaffGroup` level.
As a result all `BarLine`s of said `Score` or `StaffGroup` are
right-justified.

grobProperties.name: right-number-text
grobProperties.doc:
When the measure counter extends
over several measures (like with compressed multi-measure rests), this
is the text on the right side of the dash.  Usually unset.

grobProperties.name: right-padding
grobProperties.doc:
Space to insert on the right side
of an object (e.g., between note and its accidentals).

grobProperties.name: rotation
grobProperties.doc:
Number of degrees to rotate this object, and
what point to rotate around.  For example, `'(45 0 0)` rotates
by 45 degrees around the center of this object.

grobProperties.name: round-up-exceptions
grobProperties.doc:
A list of pairs where car is the numerator
and cdr the denominator of a moment.  Each pair in this list means that
the multi-measure rests of the corresponding length will be rounded up to
the longer rest.  See *round-up-to-longer-rest*.

grobProperties.name: round-up-to-longer-rest
grobProperties.doc:
Displays the longer multi-measure
rest when the length of a measure is between two values of
`usable-duration-logs`.  For example, displays a breve instead of a whole
in a 3/2 measure.

grobProperties.name: rounded
grobProperties.doc: Decide whether lines should be drawn rounded or not.

grobProperties.name: same-direction-correction
grobProperties.doc:
Optical correction amount
for stems that are placed in tight configurations.  This amount is
used for stems with the same direction to compensate for note head to
stem distance.

grobProperties.name: script-priority
grobProperties.doc:
A key for determining the order of
scripts in a stack, by being added to the position of the script in
the user input, the sum being the overall priority.  Smaller means
closer to the head.

grobProperties.name: segno-kern
grobProperties.doc:
The space between the two thin lines
of the segno bar line symbol, expressed as a multiple of the
default staff-line thickness (i.e., the visual output is *not*
influenced by changes to
`*Staff*.StaffSymbol.thickness`).

grobProperties.name: self-alignment-X
grobProperties.doc:
Specify alignment of an object.  The
value `-1` means left aligned, `0` centered, and
`1` right-aligned in X direction.  Other numerical
values may also be specified - the unit is half the object width.
If not a number, align on the object's reference point.

grobProperties.name: self-alignment-Y
grobProperties.doc:
Like `self-alignment-X` but for
the Y axis.

grobProperties.name: senza-misura-stencil
grobProperties.doc:
The symbol to print when
`TimeSignature@/.time-signature` is not set.  Overriding
`TimeSignature@/.stencil` circumvents this.

grobProperties.name: shape
grobProperties.doc:
This setting determines what shape a grob
has.  Valid choices depend on the `stencil` callback reading
this property.

grobProperties.name: sharp-positions
grobProperties.doc:
Sharps in key signatures are placed
within the specified ranges of staff positions.  The general form
is a list of pairs, with one pair for each type of clef, in order
of the staff position at which each clef places C:
`(alto treble tenor soprano baritone mezzosoprano bass)`.
If the list contains a single element it applies for all clefs.
A single number in place of a pair sets accidentals within the octave
ending at that staff position.

grobProperties.name: short-bar-extent
grobProperties.doc:
The Y-extent of a short bar line.  The
default is half the normal bar extent, rounded up to an integer number of staff
spaces.

grobProperties.name: shorten-pair
grobProperties.doc:
The lengths to shorten on both sides
a hairpin or text-spanner such as a pedal bracket.  Positive values
shorten the hairpin or text-spanner, while negative values lengthen
it.

grobProperties.name: shortest-duration-space
grobProperties.doc:
Start with this multiple of
`spacing-increment` space for the shortest duration.  See also
spacing-spanner-interface.

grobProperties.name: show-control-points
grobProperties.doc:
For grobs printing Bézier
curves, setting this property to `#t` causes the control points
and control polygon to be drawn on the page for ease of tweaking.

grobProperties.name: show-horizontal-skylines
grobProperties.doc:
If true, print this
grob's horizontal skylines.  This is meant for debugging purposes.

grobProperties.name: show-vertical-skylines
grobProperties.doc:
If true, print this
grob's vertical skylines.  This is meant for debugging purposes.

grobProperties.name: side-axis
grobProperties.doc:
If the value is `X` (or
equivalently `0`), the object is placed horizontally next to
the other object.  If the value is `Y` or `1`, it is
placed vertically.

grobProperties.name: side-relative-direction
grobProperties.doc:
Multiply direction of
`direction-source` with this to get the direction of this
object.

grobProperties.name: size
grobProperties.doc:
The ratio of the size of the object to its default
size.

grobProperties.name: skip-quanting
grobProperties.doc: Should beam quanting be skipped?

grobProperties.name: skyline-horizontal-padding
grobProperties.doc:
For determining the
vertical distance between two staves, it is possible to have a
configuration which would result in a tight interleaving of grobs from
the top staff and the bottom staff.  The larger this parameter is, the
farther apart the staves are placed in such a configuration.

grobProperties.name: skyline-vertical-padding
grobProperties.doc:
The amount by which the left
and right skylines of a column are padded vertically, beyond the
`Y-extent`s and `extra-spacing-height`s of the constituent
grobs in the column.  Increase this to prevent interleaving of grobs
from adjacent columns.

grobProperties.name: slash-negative-kern
grobProperties.doc:
The space to remove between
slashes in percent repeat glyphs.  Larger values bring the two
elements closer together.

grobProperties.name: slope
grobProperties.doc: The slope of this object.

grobProperties.name: slur-padding
grobProperties.doc: Extra distance between slur and script.

grobProperties.name: snap-radius
grobProperties.doc:
The maximum distance between two objects that
will cause them to snap to alignment along an axis.

grobProperties.name: space-alist
grobProperties.doc:
An alist that specifies distances from
this grob to other breakable items, using the format:

```
'((break-align-symbol . (spacing-style . space))
  (break-align-symbol . (spacing-style . space))
  ...)
```

Standard choices for `*break-align-symbol*` are listed in
Grobs and their break-align symbols.  Additionally, three
special break-align symbols available to `space-alist` are:

- `first-note`:
used when the grob is just left of the first note on a line

- `next-note`:
used when the grob is just left of any other note;
if not set, the value of `first-note` gets used

- `right-edge`:
used when the grob is the last item on the line (only compatible with
the `extra-space` spacing style)

If `space-alist` is defined for a grob that gets spaced in a
staff, an entry for `first-note` must be present.  If there
is no `next-note` entry, the value of `first-note` is
used instead.

Choices for `*spacing-style*` are:

- `extra-space`:
Put this much space between the two grobs.  The space is stretchable
and shrinkable when paired with `first-note` or `next-note`;
otherwise it is fixed.

- `minimum-space`:
Put at least this much space between the left sides of both grobs,
without allowing them to collide.  The space is stretchable and
shrinkable when paired with `first-note` or `next-note`;
otherwise it is fixed.  Not compatible with `right-edge`.

- `fixed-space`:
Only compatible with `first-note` and `next-note`.  Put
this much fixed space between the grob and the note.

- `minimum-fixed-space`:
Only compatible with `first-note` and `next-note`.  Put at
least this much fixed space between the left side of the grob and the
left side of the note, without allowing them to collide.

- `semi-fixed-space`:
Only compatible with `first-note` and `next-note`.  Put
this much space between the grob and the note, such that half of the
space is fixed and half is stretchable and shrinkable.

- `shrink-space`:
Only compatible with `first-note` and `next-note`.  Put
this much space between the two grobs.  The space is only shrinkable.

- `semi-shrink-space`:
Only compatible with `first-note` and `next-note`.  Put
this much space between the grob and the note, such that half of the
space is fixed and half is shrinkable.

Rules for this spacing are much more complicated than this.
See [Wanske] page 126--134, [Ross] page 143--147.

grobProperties.name: space-increment
grobProperties.doc:
The amount by which the total duration
of a multi-measure rest affects horizontal spacing.  Each doubling of the
duration adds `space-increment` to the length of the bar.

grobProperties.name: space-to-barline
grobProperties.doc:
If set, the distance between a note
and the following non-musical column will be measured to the bar line
instead of to the beginning of the non-musical column.  If there is a
clef change followed by a bar line, for example, this means that we
will try to space the non-musical column as though the clef is not
there.

grobProperties.name: spacing-increment
grobProperties.doc:
The unit of length for
note-spacing.  Typically, the width of a note head.  See also
spacing-spanner-interface.

grobProperties.name: spacing-pair
grobProperties.doc:
A pair of alignment symbols which set an object's
spacing relative to its left and right `BreakAlignment`s.

For example, a `MultiMeasureRest` will ignore prefatory items at its
bounds (i.e., clefs, key signatures and time signatures) using the following
override:

```
\override MultiMeasureRest.spacing-pair =
             #'(staff-bar . staff-bar)
```

grobProperties.name: span-all-note-heads
grobProperties.doc:
If true, tuplet brackets are
printed spanning horizontally from the first to the last note head
instead of covering only the stems.

grobProperties.name: spanner-id
grobProperties.doc: An identifier to distinguish concurrent spanners.

grobProperties.name: springs-and-rods
grobProperties.doc:
Dummy variable for triggering
spacing routines.

grobProperties.name: stacking-dir
grobProperties.doc: Stack objects in which direction?

grobProperties.name: staff-affinity
grobProperties.doc:
The direction of the staff to use
for spacing the current non-staff line.  Choices are `UP`,
`DOWN`, and `CENTER`.  If `CENTER`, the non-staff
line will be placed equidistant between the two nearest staves on
either side, unless collisions or other spacing constraints
prevent this.  Setting `staff-affinity` for a staff causes it
to be treated as a non-staff line.  Setting `staff-affinity`
to `#f` causes a non-staff line to be treated as a staff.

grobProperties.name: staff-padding
grobProperties.doc:
Maintain this much space between
reference points and the staff.  Its effect is to align objects of
differing sizes (like the dynamics **p** and **f**) on their
baselines.

grobProperties.name: staff-position
grobProperties.doc:
Vertical position, measured in half
staff spaces, counted from the middle line.

For ties, there is a distinction between exact and inexact values: an
exact value serves as a rough vertical offset that gets further tuned
to make the tie avoid staff lines.  An inexact value is taken as the
precise vertical offset without further adjustments.

grobProperties.name: staff-space
grobProperties.doc:
Amount of space between staff lines,
expressed in global `staff-space`.

grobProperties.name: staff-staff-spacing
grobProperties.doc:
When applied to a
staff-group's `StaffGrouper` grob, this spacing alist controls
the distance between consecutive staves within the staff-group.  When
applied to a staff's `VerticalAxisGroup` grob, it controls the
distance between the staff and the nearest staff below it in the same
system, replacing any settings inherited from the `StaffGrouper`
grob of the containing staff-group, if there is one.  This property
remains in effect even when non-staff lines appear between staves.
The alist can contain the following keys:

-
`basic-distance` -- the vertical distance, measured in
staff-spaces, between the reference points of the two items when
no collisions would result, and no stretching or compressing is in
effect.

-
`minimum-distance` -- the smallest allowable vertical
distance, measured in staff-spaces, between the reference points
of the two items, when compressing is in effect.

-
`padding` -- the minimum required amount of unobstructed
vertical whitespace between the bounding boxes (or skylines) of
the two items, measured in staff-spaces.

-
`stretchability` -- a unitless measure of the dimension's
relative propensity to stretch.  If zero, the distance will not
stretch (unless collisions would result).

grobProperties.name: staffgroup-staff-spacing
grobProperties.doc:
The spacing alist
controlling the distance between the last staff of the current
staff-group and the staff just below it in the same system, even
if one or more non-staff lines exist between the two staves.  If
the `staff-staff-spacing` property of the staff's
`VerticalAxisGroup` grob is set, that is used instead.  See
`staff-staff-spacing` for a description of the alist
structure.

grobProperties.name: stem-attachment
grobProperties.doc:
An `(*x* . *y*)` pair
where the stem attaches to the note head.  Each component is measured in
a -1 to 1 scale so that -1 is the left/bottom edge of the note's
bounding box and 1 is the right/top edge.

grobProperties.name: stem-begin-position
grobProperties.doc:
User override for the
begin position of a stem.

grobProperties.name: stem-spacing-correction
grobProperties.doc:
Optical correction amount for
stems that are placed in tight configurations.  For opposite
directions, this amount is the correction for two normal sized stems
that overlap completely.

grobProperties.name: stemlet-length
grobProperties.doc:
How long should be a stem over a
rest?

grobProperties.name: stencil
grobProperties.doc: The symbol to print.

grobProperties.name: stencils
grobProperties.doc:
Multiple stencils, used as intermediate
value.

grobProperties.name: strict-grace-spacing
grobProperties.doc:
If set, main notes are spaced
normally, then grace notes are put left of the musical columns for the
main notes.

grobProperties.name: strict-note-spacing
grobProperties.doc:
If set, unbroken columns with
non-musical material (clefs, bar lines, etc.) are not spaced
separately, but put before musical columns.

grobProperties.name: stroke-style
grobProperties.doc:
Set to `"grace"` to turn stroke
through flag on.

grobProperties.name: style
grobProperties.doc:
This setting determines in what style a grob is
typeset.  Valid choices depend on the `stencil` callback reading
this property.

grobProperties.name: text
grobProperties.doc: Text markup.  See Formatting text.

grobProperties.name: text-alignment-X
grobProperties.doc: How to align an annotation horizontally.

grobProperties.name: text-alignment-Y
grobProperties.doc: How to align an annotation vertically.

grobProperties.name: text-direction
grobProperties.doc:
This controls the ordering of the
words.  The default `RIGHT` is for roman text.  Arabic or Hebrew
should use `LEFT`.

grobProperties.name: thick-thickness
grobProperties.doc:
Thickness of the thick line in a
bar line, expressed as a multiple of the default staff-line
thickness (i.e., the visual output is *not* influenced by
changes to `*Staff*.StaffSymbol.thickness`).

grobProperties.name: thickness
grobProperties.doc:
For grobs made up of lines, this is the
thickness of the line.  For slurs and ties, this is the distance
between the two arcs of the curve's outline at its thickest point,
not counting the diameter of the virtual “pen” that draws the
arcs.  This property is expressed as a multiple of the current
staff-line thickness (i.e., the visual output is influenced by
changes to `*Staff*.StaffSymbol.thickness`).

grobProperties.name: tie-configuration
grobProperties.doc:
List of `(*position* .
*dir*)` pairs, indicating a desired tie configuration that
overrides the default.  *position* is the offset from the center
of the staff in half staff-space units, and *dir* indicates the
direction of the tie (`1`=>up, `-1`=>down,
`0`=>center).  A non-pair entry in the list causes the
corresponding tie to be formatted automatically.

There is a distinction between exact and inexact values for
*position*: an exact value serves as a rough vertical offset that
gets further tuned to make the tie avoid staff lines.  An inexact
value is taken as the precise vertical offset without further
adjustments.

grobProperties.name: time-signature
grobProperties.doc:
A time-signature specification.  See
the `\time` command.

grobProperties.name: to-barline
grobProperties.doc:
If true, the spanner will stop at the bar
line just before it would otherwise stop.

grobProperties.name: toward-stem-shift
grobProperties.doc:
Amount by which scripts are shifted
toward the stem if their direction coincides with the stem direction.
`0.0` means centered on the note head (the default position of
most scripts); `1.0` means centered on the stem.  Interpolated
values are possible.

grobProperties.name: toward-stem-shift-in-column
grobProperties.doc:
Amount by which a script
is shifted toward the stem if its direction coincides with the stem
direction and it is associated with a `ScriptColumn` object.
`0.0` means centered on the note head (the default position of
most scripts); `1.0` means centered on the stem.  Interpolated
values are possible.

grobProperties.name: transparent
grobProperties.doc: This makes the grob invisible.

grobProperties.name: tuplet-slur
grobProperties.doc:
Draw a slur instead of a bracket for
tuplets.

grobProperties.name: uniform-stretching
grobProperties.doc:
If set, items stretch
proportionally to their natural separation based on durations.
This looks better in complex polyphonic patterns.

grobProperties.name: usable-duration-logs
grobProperties.doc:
List of `duration-log`s that
can be used in typesetting the grob.

grobProperties.name: used
grobProperties.doc:
If set, this spacing column is kept in the
spacing problem.

grobProperties.name: vertical-skylines
grobProperties.doc:
Two skylines, one above and
one below this grob.

grobProperties.name: visible-over-note-heads
grobProperties.doc:
This prints a tuplet bracket
when the bracket is set to be over the note heads.  This option can
be combined with the default tuplet bracket visibility style and
with `#'if-no-beam`.

grobProperties.name: voiced-position
grobProperties.doc:
The staff position of a voiced
`Rest`, negative if the rest has `direction` `DOWN`.

grobProperties.name: volta-number-offset
grobProperties.doc:
The offset of the volta number
relative to the upper left corner of the volta bracket.

grobProperties.name: when
grobProperties.doc: Global time step associated with this column.

grobProperties.name: whiteout
grobProperties.doc:
If a number or true, the grob is
printed over a white background to white-out underlying material, if
the grob is visible.  A number indicates how far the white background
extends beyond the bounding box of the grob as a multiple of the
staff-line thickness.  The `LyricHyphen` grob uses a special
implementation of whiteout: A positive number indicates how far the
white background extends beyond the bounding box in multiples of
`line-thickness`.  The shape of the background is determined by
`whiteout-style`.

Usually `#f` by default.  If `whiteout-color` is set, use
this color instead of white for the background.

grobProperties.name: whiteout-color
grobProperties.doc:
The background color used if property
`whiteout` is set.

grobProperties.name: whiteout-style
grobProperties.doc:
Determines the shape of the
`whiteout` background.  Available are `'outline`,
`'rounded-box`, and the default `'box`.  There is one
exception: Use `'special` for `LyricHyphen`.

grobProperties.name: widened-extent
grobProperties.doc:
The vertical extent that a bar
line on a certain staff symbol should have.  If the staff symbol is
small (e.g., has just one line, as in a `RhythmicStaff`, this is
wider than the staff symbol's Y extent.

grobProperties.name: width
grobProperties.doc:
The width of a grob measured in staff
space.

grobProperties.name: woodwind-diagram-details
grobProperties.doc:
An alist of detailed
grob properties for woodwind diagrams.  Each alist entry consists of a
`(*property* . *value*)` pair.  The properties which can
be included in woodwind-diagram-details include the following:

-
`fill-angle` -- Rotation angle of a partially filled key from
horizontal. Default value 0.
-
`text-trill-circled` -- In non-graphical mode, for keys shown as
text, indicate a trill by circling the text if true, or by shading the
text if false.  Default value #t.

grobProperties.name: word-space
grobProperties.doc:
Space to insert between words in
texts.

grobProperties.name: zigzag-length
grobProperties.doc:
The length of the lines of a
zigzag, relative to `zigzag-width`.  A value of `1`
gives 60-degree zigzags.

grobProperties.name: zigzag-width
grobProperties.doc:
The width of one zigzag squiggle.
This number is adjusted slightly so that the spanner line can be
constructed from a whole number of squiggles.

contextProperties.name: aDueText
contextProperties.doc: Text to print at a unisono passage.

contextProperties.name: accidentalGrouping
contextProperties.doc:
If set to `'voice`, accidentals
on the same note in different octaves may be horizontally staggered
if in different voices.

contextProperties.name: additionalBassStrings
contextProperties.doc:
The additional tablature bass-strings, which
will not get a separate line in `TabStaff`.  It is a list of the pitches of each
string (starting with the lowest numbered one).

contextProperties.name: additionalPitchPrefix
contextProperties.doc:
Text with which to prefix
additional pitches within a chord name.

contextProperties.name: alignAboveContext
contextProperties.doc:
Where to insert newly created context in
vertical alignment.

contextProperties.name: alignBelowContext
contextProperties.doc:
Where to insert newly created context in
vertical alignment.

contextProperties.name: alterationGlyphs
contextProperties.doc:
Alist mapping alterations to accidental glyphs.
Alterations are given as exact numbers, e.g., -1/2 for flat.  This applies
to all grobs that can print accidentals.

contextProperties.name: alternativeNumber
contextProperties.doc:
When set, the first volta number for the
current `\alternative` element.  Not set outside of alternatives.

contextProperties.name: alternativeNumberingStyle
contextProperties.doc:
The scheme and style for
numbering bars in repeat alternatives.  If not set (the default), bar
numbers continue through alternatives.  Can be set to `numbers`
to reset the bar number at each alternative, or set to
`numbers-with-letters` to reset and also include letter
suffixes.

contextProperties.name: alternativeRestores
contextProperties.doc:
Timing variables that are
restored to their value at the start of the first alternative in
subsequent alternatives.

contextProperties.name: associatedVoice
contextProperties.doc:
Name of the context (see
`associatedVoiceType` for its type, usually `Voice`) that
has the melody for this `Lyrics` line.

contextProperties.name: associatedVoiceType
contextProperties.doc:
Type of the context that has the
melody for this `Lyrics` line.

contextProperties.name: autoAccidentals
contextProperties.doc:
List of different ways to typeset an
accidental.

For determining when to print an accidental, several different rules
are tried.  The rule that gives the highest number of accidentals is
used.

Each entry in the list is either a symbol or a procedure.

- *symbol*:
The symbol is the name of the context in which the following rules are to be
applied.  For example, if *context* is Score then all
staves share accidentals, and if *context* is Staff then
all voices in the same staff share accidentals, but staves do not.

- *procedure*:
The procedure represents an accidental rule to be applied to the previously
specified context.

The procedure takes the following arguments:

- `context`:
The current context to which the rule should be applied.

- `pitch`:
The pitch of the note to be evaluated.

- `barnum`:
The current bar number.

The procedure returns a pair of Booleans.  The first states whether an extra
natural should be added.  The second states whether an accidental should be
printed.  `(#t . #f)` does not make sense.

contextProperties.name: autoBeamCheck
contextProperties.doc:
A procedure taking three
arguments, *context*, *dir* [start/@/stop (-1 or 1)], and
*test* [shortest note in the beam].  A non-`#f` return value
starts or stops the auto beam.

contextProperties.name: autoBeaming
contextProperties.doc:
If set to `#t` then beams are generated
automatically.  If set to `#f`, auto-beaming is switched off as soon as the
current beam (if any) is finished according to the auto-beaming rules.

contextProperties.name: autoCautionaries
contextProperties.doc:
List similar to `autoAccidentals`,
but it controls cautionary accidentals rather than normal ones.  Both
lists are tried, and the one giving the most accidentals wins.  In
case of draw, a normal accidental is typeset.

contextProperties.name: autoExtenders
contextProperties.doc:
Create lyric extenders automatically for
syllables in melismata that are not followed by a hyphen.

contextProperties.name: barExtraVelocity
contextProperties.doc:
Extra MIDI velocity added by the
`Beat_performer` at the start of each measure.

contextProperties.name: barNumberFormatter
contextProperties.doc:
A procedure that takes a bar
number, measure position, and alternative number and returns a markup
of the bar number to print.

contextProperties.name: barNumberVisibility
contextProperties.doc:
A procedure that takes a bar
number and a measure position and returns whether the corresponding
bar number should be printed.  Note that the actual print-out of
bar numbers is controlled with the `break-visibility` property.

The following procedures are predefined:

- `all-bar-numbers-visible`:
Enable bar numbers for all bars, including the first one and broken
bars (which get bar numbers in parentheses).

- `first-bar-number-invisible`:
Enable bar numbers for all bars (including broken bars) except the
first one.  If the first bar is broken, it doesn't get a bar number
either.

- `first-bar-number-invisible-save-broken-bars`:
Enable bar numbers for all bars (including broken bars) except the
first one.  A broken first bar gets a bar number.

- `first-bar-number-invisible-and-no-parenthesized-bar-numbers`:
Enable bar numbers for all bars except the first bar and broken bars.
This is the default.

- `(every-nth-bar-number-visible *n*)`:
Assuming *n* is value 2, for example, this enables bar numbers
for bars 2, 4, 6, etc.

- `(modulo-bar-number-visible *n* *m*)`:
If bar numbers 1, 4, 7, etc., should be enabled, *n* (the modulo)
must be set to 3 and *m* (the division remainder) to 1.

contextProperties.name: beamExceptions
contextProperties.doc:
An alist of exceptions to auto-beam rules
that normally end on beats.

contextProperties.name: beamHalfMeasure
contextProperties.doc:
Whether to allow a beam to begin
halfway through the measure in triple time, which could look like 6/8.

contextProperties.name: beamMaximumSubdivision
contextProperties.doc:
Maximum
interval to subdivide beams, limiting the depth of beamlets removed from
subdivision. Ranges from 0 to infinity ( `0`=no subdivision,
`+inf.0`=no limit).

contextProperties.name: beamMinimumSubdivision
contextProperties.doc:
Minimum
interval to subdivide beams, ignoring beamlets whose subdivision depth is too
shallow. Ranges from 0 to infinity ( `0`=no limit,
`+inf.0`=no subdivision).

contextProperties.name: beatBase
contextProperties.doc:
The musical length
corresponding to one unit of `beatStructure`.

contextProperties.name: beatExtraVelocity
contextProperties.doc:
Extra MIDI velocity added by the
`Beat_performer` at the start of each beat.

contextProperties.name: beatStructure
contextProperties.doc:
A sequence describing the length of each beat
in the measure in units of `beatBase`.

contextProperties.name: breathMarkType
contextProperties.doc:
The type of `BreathingSign` to create at
`\breathe`.

contextProperties.name: caesuraType
contextProperties.doc:
An alist

```
((bar-line . bar-type)
 (breath . breath-type)
 (scripts . script-type…)
 (underlying-bar-line . bar-type))
```

specifying which breath mark, bar line, and scripts to create at
`\caesura`.  All entries are optional.

`bar-@/line` has higher priority than a measure bar line and
`underlying-@/bar-@/line` has lower priority than a measure bar
line.

contextProperties.name: caesuraTypeTransform
contextProperties.doc:
An engraver callback taking
three arguments and returning an alist of the same kind as
`caesuraType`.

The first argument is the context.

The second argument is the value of `caesuraType` with an
additional entry `(articulations . *symbol-@/list*)`
identifying the articulations attached to the caesura in the music.
If the transform function returns this second argument unmodified, it
is as if no transform function were set; the function is free to
return a different value.  The transform function can remove
articulations, but any added articulations are ignored.

The third argument is a symbol-list identifying certain things the
engraver has observed.  `bar-@/line` indicates that the engraver
has observed a `BarLine` at the current moment.

contextProperties.name: centerBarNumbers
contextProperties.doc:
Whether to center bar numbers in
their measure instead of aligning them on the bar line.

contextProperties.name: chordChanges
contextProperties.doc: Only show changes in chords scheme?

contextProperties.name: chordNameExceptions
contextProperties.doc:
An alist of chord exceptions.
Contains `(*chord* . *markup*)` entries.

contextProperties.name: chordNameFunction
contextProperties.doc:
The function that converts lists
of pitches to chord names.

contextProperties.name: chordNameLowercaseMinor
contextProperties.doc: Downcase roots of minor chords?

contextProperties.name: chordNameSeparator
contextProperties.doc:
The markup object used to
separate parts of a chord name.

contextProperties.name: chordNoteNamer
contextProperties.doc:
A function that converts from a pitch
object to a text markup.  Used for single pitches.

contextProperties.name: chordPrefixSpacer
contextProperties.doc:
The space added between the root
symbol and the prefix of a chord name.

contextProperties.name: chordRootNamer
contextProperties.doc:
A function that converts from a pitch
object to a text markup.  Used for chords.

contextProperties.name: clefGlyph
contextProperties.doc: Name of the symbol within the music font.

contextProperties.name: clefPosition
contextProperties.doc:
Where should the center of the clef
symbol go, measured in half staff spaces from the center of the
staff.

contextProperties.name: clefTransposition
contextProperties.doc:
Add this much extra transposition to a
clef.  Values of 7 and -7 are common.

contextProperties.name: clefTranspositionFormatter
contextProperties.doc:
A procedure that takes the
transposition number of a `Clef` grob as a string and the style as a
symbol and returns a markup.

contextProperties.name: clefTranspositionStyle
contextProperties.doc:
Determines the way the
`ClefModifier` grob of a clef is displayed.  Possible values are
`'default`, `'parenthesized`, and `'bracketed`.

contextProperties.name: codaMarkFormatter
contextProperties.doc:
A procedure that creates a coda
mark (which in conventional *D.S. al Coda* form indicates the
start of the alternative endings), taking as arguments the mark
sequence number and the context.  It should return a markup object.

contextProperties.name: completionBusy
contextProperties.doc: Whether a completion-note head is playing.

contextProperties.name: completionFactor
contextProperties.doc:
When `Completion_heads_engraver` and
`Completion_rest_engraver` need to split a note or rest with a
scaled duration, such as `c2*3`, this specifies the scale factor
to use for the newly-split notes and rests created by the engraver.

If `#f`, the completion engraver uses the scale-factor of
each duration being split.

If set to a callback procedure, that procedure is called with the
context of the completion engraver, and the duration to be split.

contextProperties.name: completionUnit
contextProperties.doc:
Sub-bar unit of
completion.

contextProperties.name: connectArpeggios
contextProperties.doc:
If set, connect arpeggios across
piano staff.

contextProperties.name: connectChordBrackets
contextProperties.doc:
If set, connect chord brackets across
piano staff.

contextProperties.name: connectChordSlurs
contextProperties.doc:
If set, connect chord slurs across piano
staff.

contextProperties.name: countPercentRepeats
contextProperties.doc:
If set, produce counters for
percent repeats.

contextProperties.name: createKeyOnClefChange
contextProperties.doc:
Print a key signature whenever
the clef is changed.

contextProperties.name: createSpacing
contextProperties.doc:
Create `StaffSpacing` objects?
Should be set for staves.

contextProperties.name: crescendoSpanner
contextProperties.doc:
The type of spanner to be used for
crescendi.  Available values are `hairpin` and `text`.  If unset,
a hairpin crescendo is used.

contextProperties.name: crescendoText
contextProperties.doc:
The text to print at start of non-hairpin
crescendo, i.e., `cresc.`.

contextProperties.name: cueClefGlyph
contextProperties.doc: Name of the symbol within the music font.

contextProperties.name: cueClefPosition
contextProperties.doc:
Where should the center of the clef
symbol go, measured in half staff spaces from the center of the
staff.

contextProperties.name: cueClefTransposition
contextProperties.doc:
Add this much extra transposition to
a cue clef.  Values of 7 and -7 are common.

contextProperties.name: cueClefTranspositionFormatter
contextProperties.doc:
A procedure that takes
the transposition number of a `cueClef` grob as a string and the style as a
symbol and returns a markup.

contextProperties.name: cueClefTranspositionStyle
contextProperties.doc:
Determines the way the
`ClefModifier` grob of a cue clef is displayed.  Possible values are
`'default`, `'parenthesized`, and `'bracketed`.

contextProperties.name: currentBarNumber
contextProperties.doc:
Contains the current bar number.
This property is incremented at every bar line.

contextProperties.name: dalSegnoTextFormatter
contextProperties.doc:
Format a jump instruction
such as *D.S.*

The first argument is the context.

The second argument is the number of times the instruction is
performed.

The third argument is a list of three markups: *start-markup*,
*end-markup*, and *next-markup*.

If *start-markup* is `#f`, the form is *da capo*;
otherwise the form is *dal segno* and *start-markup* is the
sign at the start of the repeated section.

If *end-markup* is not `#f`, it is either the sign at the end
of the main body of the repeat, or it is a *Fine* instruction.
When it is a Fine instruction, *next-markup* is `#f`.

If *next-markup* is not `#f`, it is the mark to be jumped to
after performing the body of the repeat, e.g., Coda.

contextProperties.name: decrescendoSpanner
contextProperties.doc:
The type of spanner to be used for
decrescendi.  Available values are `hairpin` and `text`.  If
unset, a hairpin decrescendo is used.

contextProperties.name: decrescendoText
contextProperties.doc:
The text to print at start of
non-hairpin decrescendo, i.e., `dim.`.

contextProperties.name: defaultStrings
contextProperties.doc:
A list of strings to use in calculating
frets for tablatures and fretboards if no strings are provided in
the notes for the current moment.

contextProperties.name: doubleRepeatBarType
contextProperties.doc:
Bar line to insert where the end
of one `\repeat volta` coincides with the start of another.  The
default is `:..:`.

contextProperties.name: doubleRepeatSegnoBarType
contextProperties.doc:
Bar line to insert where an
in-staff segno coincides with the end of one `\repeat volta` and
the beginning of another.  The default is `:|.S.|:`.

contextProperties.name: doubleSlurs
contextProperties.doc:
If set, two slurs are created for every
slurred note, one above and one below the chord.

contextProperties.name: drumPitchTable
contextProperties.doc:
A table mapping percussion
instruments (symbols) to pitches.

contextProperties.name: drumStyleTable
contextProperties.doc:
A hash table which maps drums to
layout settings.  Predefined values: `drums-style`,
`agostini-drums-style`, `weinberg-drums-style`,
`timbales-style`, `congas-style`,
`bongos-style`, and `percussion-style`.

The layout style is a hash table, containing the drum-pitches (e.g.,
the symbol `hihat`) as keys, and a list
`(*notehead-style* *script* *vertical-position*)` as
values.

contextProperties.name: endAtSkip
contextProperties.doc: End `DurationLine` grob on `skip-event`

contextProperties.name: endRepeatBarType
contextProperties.doc:
Bar line to insert at the end of a
`\repeat volta`.  The default is `:|.`.

contextProperties.name: endRepeatSegnoBarType
contextProperties.doc:
Bar line to insert where an in-staff
segno coincides with the end of a `\repeat volta`.  The default is
`:|.S`.

contextProperties.name: explicitClefVisibility
contextProperties.doc:
`break-visibility`
function for clef changes.

contextProperties.name: explicitCueClefVisibility
contextProperties.doc:
`break-visibility`
function for cue clef changes.

contextProperties.name: explicitKeySignatureVisibility
contextProperties.doc:
`break-visibility`
function for explicit key changes.  `\override` of the
`break-visibility` property will set the visibility for
normal (i.e., at the start of the line) key signatures.

contextProperties.name: extendersOverRests
contextProperties.doc:
Whether to continue extenders as
they cross a rest.

contextProperties.name: extraNatural
contextProperties.doc:
Whether to typeset an extra natural sign
before accidentals that reduce the effect of a previous alteration.

contextProperties.name: figuredBassAlterationDirection
contextProperties.doc:
Where to put alterations
relative to the main figure.

contextProperties.name: figuredBassCenterContinuations
contextProperties.doc:
Whether to vertically
center pairs of extender lines.  This does not work with three or more
lines.

contextProperties.name: figuredBassFormatter
contextProperties.doc:
A routine generating a markup
for a bass figure.

contextProperties.name: figuredBassLargeNumberAlignment
contextProperties.doc:
Horizontal alignment
to use for numbers in figured bass that contain more than a single
digit.

contextProperties.name: figuredBassPlusDirection
contextProperties.doc:
Where to put plus signs
relative to the main figure.

contextProperties.name: figuredBassPlusStrokedAlist
contextProperties.doc:
An alist mapping figured
bass digits to glyphs.  The default is mapping numbers 2, 4, 5, 6, 7,
and 9 to the six glyphs `figbass.*plus` and
`figbass.*stroked`, respectively.

contextProperties.name: finalFineTextVisibility
contextProperties.doc:
Whether `\fine` at the
written end of the music should create a *Fine* instruction.

contextProperties.name: fineBarType
contextProperties.doc:
Bar line to insert at `\fine`.
Where there is also a repeat bar line, the repeat bar line takes
precedence and this value is appended to it as an annotation.  The
default is `|.`.

contextProperties.name: fineSegnoBarType
contextProperties.doc:
Bar line to insert where an in-staff
segno coincides with `\fine`.  The default is `|.S`.

contextProperties.name: fineStartRepeatSegnoBarType
contextProperties.doc:
Bar line to insert where
an in-staff segno coincides with `\fine` and the start of a
`\repeat volta`.  The default is `|.S.|:`.

contextProperties.name: fineText
contextProperties.doc: The text to print at `\fine`.

contextProperties.name: fingeringOrientations
contextProperties.doc:
A list of symbols, containing
`left`, `right`, `up` and/@/or `down`.  This list
determines where fingerings are put relative to the chord being
fingered.

contextProperties.name: firstClef
contextProperties.doc:
If true, create a new clef when starting a
staff.

contextProperties.name: followVoice
contextProperties.doc:
If set, note heads are tracked across
staff switches by a thin line.

contextProperties.name: fontSize
contextProperties.doc: The relative size of all grobs in a context.

contextProperties.name: forbidBreak
contextProperties.doc:
If set to `#t`, prevent a line break
at this point, except if explicitly requested by the user.

contextProperties.name: forbidBreakBetweenBarLines
contextProperties.doc:
If set to `#t`,
`Bar_@/engraver` forbids line breaks where there is no bar line.

contextProperties.name: forceClef
contextProperties.doc:
Show clef symbol, even if it has not
changed.  Only active for the first clef after the property is set, not
for the full staff.

contextProperties.name: fretLabels
contextProperties.doc:
A list of strings or Scheme-formatted markups
containing, in the correct order, the labels to be used for lettered
frets in tablature.

contextProperties.name: glissandoMap
contextProperties.doc:
A map in the form of
`'((source1 . target1) (source2 . target2) ... (source*n* .
target*n*))`, showing the glissandi to be drawn for note columns.
The value `'()` defaults to `'((0 . 0) (1 . 1) ... (*n* .
*n*))`, where *n* is the minimum number of note heads in
the two note columns between which the glissandi occur.

contextProperties.name: gridInterval
contextProperties.doc:
Interval for which to
generate `GridPoint`s.

contextProperties.name: handleNegativeFrets
contextProperties.doc:
How the automatic fret calculator
should handle calculated negative frets.  Values include `'ignore`,
to leave them out of the diagram completely, `'include`, to include
them as calculated, and `'recalculate`, to ignore the specified
string and find a string where they will fit with a positive fret number.

contextProperties.name: harmonicAccidentals
contextProperties.doc:
If set, harmonic notes in chords
get accidentals.

contextProperties.name: harmonicDots
contextProperties.doc:
If set, harmonic notes in dotted chords get
dots.

contextProperties.name: highStringOne
contextProperties.doc:
Whether the first string is the string
with highest pitch on the instrument.  This used by the automatic
string selector for tablature notation.

contextProperties.name: ignoreBarChecks
contextProperties.doc: Ignore bar checks.

contextProperties.name: ignoreBarNumberChecks
contextProperties.doc: Ignore bar number checks.

contextProperties.name: ignoreFiguredBassRest
contextProperties.doc: Don't swallow rest events.

contextProperties.name: ignoreMelismata
contextProperties.doc:
Ignore melismata for this
Lyrics line.

contextProperties.name: implicitBassFigures
contextProperties.doc:
A list of bass figures that are not
printed as numbers, but only as extender lines.

contextProperties.name: includeGraceNotes
contextProperties.doc:
Do not ignore grace notes for
Lyrics.

contextProperties.name: initialTimeSignatureVisibility
contextProperties.doc:
break visibility for
the initial time signature.

contextProperties.name: instrumentCueName
contextProperties.doc:
The name to print if another
instrument is to be taken.

This property is deprecated

contextProperties.name: instrumentEqualizer
contextProperties.doc:
A function taking a
string (instrument name), and returning a `(*min* . *max*)`
pair of numbers for the loudness range of the instrument.

contextProperties.name: instrumentName
contextProperties.doc:
The name to print left of a staff.  The
`instrumentName` property labels the staff in the first system, and
the `shortInstrumentName` property labels following lines.

contextProperties.name: instrumentTransposition
contextProperties.doc:
Define the transposition of
the instrument. Its value is the pitch that sounds when the instrument
plays written middle C.  This is used to transpose the MIDI output,
and `\quote`s.

contextProperties.name: internalBarNumber
contextProperties.doc:
Contains the current bar number.
This property is used for internal timekeeping, among others by the
`Accidental_engraver`.

contextProperties.name: keepAliveInterfaces
contextProperties.doc:
A list of symbols, signifying grob
interfaces that are worth keeping a staff with `remove-empty` set
around for.

contextProperties.name: keyAlterationOrder
contextProperties.doc:
A list of pairs that defines in what
order alterations should be printed.  The format of an entry is
`(*step* . *alter*)`,
where *step* is a number from 0 to 6 and
*alter* from -1 (double flat) to 1 (double sharp),
with exact rationals for alterations in between, e.g., 1/2
for sharp.

contextProperties.name: keyAlterations
contextProperties.doc:
The current key signature.  This is an alist
containing `(*step* . *alter*)` or
`((*octave* . *step*) . *alter*)`, where *step*
is a number in the range 0 to 6 and *alter* a fraction,
denoting alteration.  For alterations, use symbols, e.g.,
`keyAlterations = #'((6 . ,FLAT))`.

contextProperties.name: lyricMelismaAlignment
contextProperties.doc: Alignment to use for a melisma syllable.

contextProperties.name: lyricRepeatCountFormatter
contextProperties.doc:
A procedure taking as
arguments the context and the numeric repeat count.  It should return
the formatted repeat count as markup.  If it does not return markup,
no grob is created.

contextProperties.name: magnifyStaffValue
contextProperties.doc:
The most recent value set with
`\magnifyStaff`.

contextProperties.name: majorSevenSymbol
contextProperties.doc:
How should the major 7th be formatted
in a chord name?

contextProperties.name: maximumFretStretch
contextProperties.doc:
Don't allocate frets further than
this from specified frets.

contextProperties.name: measureBarType
contextProperties.doc: Bar line to insert at a measure boundary.

contextProperties.name: measureLength
contextProperties.doc:
The musical length of
the current measure.

contextProperties.name: melismaBusyProperties
contextProperties.doc:
A list of properties (symbols) to
determine whether a melisma is playing.  Setting this property will
influence how lyrics are aligned to notes.  For example, if set to
`'(melismaBusy beamMelismaBusy)`, only manual melismata and
manual beams are considered.  Possible values include
`melismaBusy`, `slurMelismaBusy`, `tieMelismaBusy`, and
`beamMelismaBusy`.

contextProperties.name: metronomeMarkFormatter
contextProperties.doc:
How to produce a metronome
markup.  Called with two arguments: a `TempoChangeEvent` and context.

contextProperties.name: middleCClefPosition
contextProperties.doc:
The position of the middle C,
as determined only by the clef.  This can be calculated by looking at
`clefPosition` and `clefGlyph`.

contextProperties.name: middleCCuePosition
contextProperties.doc:
The position of the middle C,
as determined only by the clef of the cue notes.  This can be calculated by
looking at `cueClefPosition` and `cueClefGlyph`.

contextProperties.name: middleCOffset
contextProperties.doc:
The offset of
middle C from the position given by `middleCClefPosition` This
is used for ottava brackets.

contextProperties.name: middleCPosition
contextProperties.doc:
The place of the middle C, measured in
half staff-spaces.  Usually determined by looking at
`middleCClefPosition` and `middleCOffset`.

contextProperties.name: midiBalance
contextProperties.doc:
Stereo balance for the MIDI channel
associated with the current context.  Ranges from -1 to 1,
where the values -1 (`#LEFT`), 0 (`#CENTER`)
and 1 (`#RIGHT`) correspond to leftmost emphasis, center
balance, and rightmost emphasis, respectively.

contextProperties.name: midiChannelMapping
contextProperties.doc:
How to map MIDI channels: per
`staff` (default), `instrument` or `voice`.

contextProperties.name: midiChorusLevel
contextProperties.doc:
Chorus effect level for the MIDI
channel associated with the current context.  Ranges from 0
to 1 (0=off, 1=full effect).

contextProperties.name: midiExpression
contextProperties.doc:
Expression control for the MIDI
channel associated with the current context.  Ranges from 0
to 1 (0=off, 1=full effect).

contextProperties.name: midiInstrument
contextProperties.doc: Name of the MIDI instrument to use.

contextProperties.name: midiMaximumVolume
contextProperties.doc:
Analogous to
`midiMinimumVolume`.

contextProperties.name: midiMergeUnisons
contextProperties.doc:
If true, output only one MIDI note-on
event when notes with the same pitch, in the same MIDI-file track, overlap.

contextProperties.name: midiMinimumVolume
contextProperties.doc:
Set the minimum loudness for MIDI.
Ranges from 0 to 1.

contextProperties.name: midiPanPosition
contextProperties.doc:
Pan position for the MIDI channel
associated with the current context.  Ranges from -1 to 1,
where the values -1 (`#LEFT`), 0 (`#CENTER`)
and 1 (`#RIGHT`) correspond to hard left, center, and hard
right, respectively.

contextProperties.name: midiReverbLevel
contextProperties.doc:
Reverb effect level for the MIDI
channel associated with the current context.  Ranges from 0
to 1 (0=off, 1=full effect).

contextProperties.name: minimumFret
contextProperties.doc:
The tablature auto string-selecting
mechanism selects the highest string with a fret at least
`minimumFret`.

contextProperties.name: minorChordModifier
contextProperties.doc:
Markup displayed following the root
for a minor chord

contextProperties.name: noChordSymbol
contextProperties.doc:
Markup to be displayed for rests in a
ChordNames context.

contextProperties.name: noteNameFunction
contextProperties.doc:
Function used to convert pitches
into strings and markups.

contextProperties.name: noteNameSeparator
contextProperties.doc:
String used to separate simultaneous
NoteName objects.

contextProperties.name: noteToFretFunction
contextProperties.doc:
Convert list of notes and list of
defined strings to full list of strings and fret numbers.
Parameters: The context, a list of note events, a list of
tabstring events, and the fretboard grob if a fretboard is desired.

contextProperties.name: nullAccidentals
contextProperties.doc:
The `Accidental_engraver`
generates no accidentals for notes in contexts were this is set.
In addition to suppressing the printed accidental, this option removes
any effect the note would have had on accidentals in other voices.

contextProperties.name: ottavaStartNow
contextProperties.doc:
Is an ottava starting in this
time step?

contextProperties.name: ottavation
contextProperties.doc:
If set, the text for an ottava spanner.
Changing this creates a new text spanner.

contextProperties.name: ottavationMarkups
contextProperties.doc:
An alist defining the markups used
for ottava brackets.  It contains entries of the form
`(*number of octaves* . *markup*)`.

contextProperties.name: output
contextProperties.doc:
The output produced by a score-level
translator during music interpretation.

contextProperties.name: pageTurnMinimumRepeatLength
contextProperties.doc:
Minimum length of
a repeated section for a page turn to be allowed within that section.

contextProperties.name: pageTurnMinimumRestLength
contextProperties.doc:
Minimum length of a
rest for a page turn to be allowed.

contextProperties.name: partCombineForced
contextProperties.doc:
Override for the `\partCombine`
decision.  Can be `apart`, `chords`, `unisono`,
`solo1`, or `solo2`.

contextProperties.name: partCombineTextsOnNote
contextProperties.doc:
Print part-combine texts only on
the next note rather than immediately on rests or skips.

contextProperties.name: pedalSostenutoStrings
contextProperties.doc: See `pedalSustainStrings`.

contextProperties.name: pedalSostenutoStyle
contextProperties.doc: See `pedalSustainStyle`.

contextProperties.name: pedalSustainStrings
contextProperties.doc:
A list of strings to print for
sustain-pedal.  Format is `(*up* *updown* *down*)`,
where each of the three is the string to print when this is done with
the pedal.

contextProperties.name: pedalSustainStyle
contextProperties.doc:
A symbol that indicates how to print
sustain pedals: `text`, `bracket` or `mixed` (both).

contextProperties.name: pedalUnaCordaStrings
contextProperties.doc: See `pedalSustainStrings`.

contextProperties.name: pedalUnaCordaStyle
contextProperties.doc: See `pedalSustainStyle`.

contextProperties.name: predefinedDiagramTable
contextProperties.doc:
The hash table of predefined
fret diagrams to use in FretBoards.

contextProperties.name: printAccidentalNames
contextProperties.doc:
Print accidentals in the
`NoteNames` context.

contextProperties.name: printInitialRepeatBar
contextProperties.doc:
Use a special bar line at the
start of a volta repeat even at the beginning of the piece.

contextProperties.name: printKeyCancellation
contextProperties.doc:
Print restoration alterations
before a key signature change.

contextProperties.name: printNotesLanguage
contextProperties.doc:
Use a specific language in the
`NoteNames` context.

contextProperties.name: printOctaveNames
contextProperties.doc:
Print octave marks in the
`NoteNames` context.

contextProperties.name: printPartCombineTexts
contextProperties.doc:
Set ‘Solo’ and ‘A due’ texts
in the part combiner?

contextProperties.name: printTrivialVoltaRepeats
contextProperties.doc:
Notate volta-style repeats even when
the repeat count is 1.

contextProperties.name: proportionalNotationDuration
contextProperties.doc:
Global override
for shortest-playing duration.  This is used for switching on proportional
notation.

contextProperties.name: rehearsalMark
contextProperties.doc: The next rehearsal mark to print.

contextProperties.name: rehearsalMarkFormatter
contextProperties.doc:
A procedure taking as
arguments the context and the sequence number of the rehearsal mark.
It should return the formatted mark as a markup object.

contextProperties.name: repeatCommands
contextProperties.doc:
A list of commands related to volta-style
repeats.  In general, each element is a list, `'(*command*
*args…*)`, but a command with no arguments may be
abbreviated to a symbol; e.g., `'((start-@/repeat))` may be given
as `'(start-@/repeat)`.

- `end-repeat *return-count*`:
End a repeated section.  *return-count* is the number of times to go back
from this point to the beginning of the section.

- `start-repeat *repeat-count*`:
Start a repeated section.  *repeat-count* is the number of times to perform
this section.

- `volta *text*`:
If *text* is markup, start a volta bracket with that label; if
*text* is `#f`, end a volta bracket.

contextProperties.name: repeatCountVisibility
contextProperties.doc:
A procedure taking as
arguments an integer and context, returning whether the corresponding
percent repeat number should be printed when `countPercentRepeats`
is set.

contextProperties.name: respectIncompleteBeams
contextProperties.doc:
When subdividing beams, limit
the beam subdivision interval until it is less than or equal to the
remaining length from the current moment. Note that it is somewhat
unclear whether to treat incomplete beams specially or not in beam
subdivision is the correct way of valid notation. The default value
of false is said to be the correct option, although beam subdivision
as if this property is true is not unpopular.

contextProperties.name: restCompletionBusy
contextProperties.doc: Signal whether a completion-rest is active.

contextProperties.name: restNumberThreshold
contextProperties.doc:
If a multi-measure rest has more
measures than this, a number is printed.

contextProperties.name: restrainOpenStrings
contextProperties.doc:
Exclude open strings from the
automatic fret calculator.

contextProperties.name: searchForVoice
contextProperties.doc:
Signal whether a search should be made
of all contexts in the context hierarchy for a voice to provide rhythms
for the lyrics.

contextProperties.name: sectionBarType
contextProperties.doc:
Bar line to insert at `\section`.
Where there is also a repeat bar line, the repeat bar line takes
precedence and this value is appended to it as an annotation.  The
default is `||`.

contextProperties.name: segnoBarType
contextProperties.doc:
Bar line to insert at an in-staff segno.
The default is `S`.

contextProperties.name: segnoMarkFormatter
contextProperties.doc:
A procedure that creates a
segno (which conventionally indicates the start of a repeated
section), taking as arguments the mark sequence number and the
context.  It should return a markup object.

contextProperties.name: segnoStyle
contextProperties.doc:
A symbol that indicates how to print a segno:
`bar-line` or `mark`.

contextProperties.name: shapeNoteStyles
contextProperties.doc:
Vector of symbols, listing style for
each note head relative to the tonic (q.v.) of the scale.

contextProperties.name: shortInstrumentName
contextProperties.doc: See `instrumentName`.

contextProperties.name: shortVocalName
contextProperties.doc: Name of a vocal line, short version.

contextProperties.name: skipBars
contextProperties.doc:
If set to `#t`, then skip the empty bars
that are produced by multi-measure notes and rests.  These bars will
not appear on the printed output.  If not set (the default),
multi-measure notes and rests expand into their full length, printing
the appropriate number of empty bars so that synchronization with other
voices is preserved.

```
{
  r1 r1*3 R1*3
  \set Score.skipBars= ##t
  r1*3 R1*3
}
```

contextProperties.name: skipTypesetting
contextProperties.doc:
If true, no typesetting is done,
speeding up the interpretation phase.  Useful for debugging large
scores.

contextProperties.name: slashChordSeparator
contextProperties.doc:
The markup object used to separate
a chord name from its root note in case of inversions or slash
chords.

contextProperties.name: soloIIText
contextProperties.doc:
The text for the start of a solo for
voice ‘two’ when part-combining.

contextProperties.name: soloText
contextProperties.doc:
The text for the start of a solo when
part-combining.

contextProperties.name: squashedPosition
contextProperties.doc:
Vertical position of squashing for
Pitch_squash_engraver.

contextProperties.name: staffLineLayoutFunction
contextProperties.doc:
Layout of staff lines,
`traditional`, or `semitone`.

contextProperties.name: stanza
contextProperties.doc:
Stanza ‘number’ to print before the start of a
verse.  Use in `Lyrics` context.

contextProperties.name: startAtNoteColumn
contextProperties.doc:
Start `DurationLine` grob at entire
`NoteColumn`.

contextProperties.name: startAtSkip
contextProperties.doc:
Start `DurationLine` grob at
`skip-event`.

contextProperties.name: startRepeatBarType
contextProperties.doc:
Bar line to insert at the start of
a `\repeat volta`.  The default is `.|:`.

contextProperties.name: startRepeatSegnoBarType
contextProperties.doc:
Bar line to insert where an
in-staff segno coincides with the start of a `\repeat volta`.
The default is `S.|:`.

contextProperties.name: stemLeftBeamCount
contextProperties.doc:
Specify the number of beams to draw
on the left side of the next note.  Overrides automatic beaming.  The
value is only used once, and then it is erased.

contextProperties.name: stemRightBeamCount
contextProperties.doc: See `stemLeftBeamCount`.

contextProperties.name: strictBeatBeaming
contextProperties.doc:
Should partial beams reflect the
beat structure even if it causes flags to hang out?

contextProperties.name: stringNumberOrientations
contextProperties.doc:
See
`fingeringOrientations`.

contextProperties.name: stringOneTopmost
contextProperties.doc:
Whether the first string is
printed on the top line of the tablature.

contextProperties.name: stringTunings
contextProperties.doc:
The tablature strings tuning.  It is a list
of the pitches of each string (starting with the lowest numbered
one).

contextProperties.name: strokeFingerOrientations
contextProperties.doc:
See
`fingeringOrientations`.

contextProperties.name: subdivideBeams
contextProperties.doc:
If set, beams of multiple stems may be
subdivided by omitting a number of beamlets, dependent on
`beamMaximumSubdivision`, between beats at multiples of
`beamMinimumSubdivision`.

contextProperties.name: submeasureBarType
contextProperties.doc:
Bar line to insert at submeasure boundaries
specified by `submeasureStructure`, when `submeasureBarsEnabled`
allows.

contextProperties.name: submeasureStructure
contextProperties.doc:
A sequence describing subdivisions of a
measure.  Each element tells the distance from the previous division in units of
`beatBase`.

contextProperties.name: suggestAccidentals
contextProperties.doc:
If set to `#t`,
accidentals are typeset as suggestions above the note.  Setting it to
`'cautionary` only applies that to cautionary accidentals.

contextProperties.name: supportNonIntegerFret
contextProperties.doc:
If set in `Score` the
`TabStaff` will print micro-tones as `2½`

contextProperties.name: suspendMelodyDecisions
contextProperties.doc:
When using the `Melody_engraver`,
stop changing orientation of stems based on the melody when this is set
to `#t`.

contextProperties.name: suspendRestMerging
contextProperties.doc:
When using the Merge_rest_engraver do not
merge rests when this is set to `#t`.

contextProperties.name: systemStartDelimiter
contextProperties.doc:
Which grob to make for the start
of the system/@/staff?  Set to `SystemStartBrace`,
`SystemStartBracket` or `SystemStartBar`.

contextProperties.name: systemStartDelimiterHierarchy
contextProperties.doc:
A nested list, indicating
the nesting of a start delimiters.

contextProperties.name: tabFullNotation
contextProperties.doc: Flag whether `\tabFullNotation` is used

contextProperties.name: tabStaffLineLayoutFunction
contextProperties.doc:
A function determining the
staff position of a tablature note head.  Called with two arguments:
the context and the string.

contextProperties.name: tablatureFormat
contextProperties.doc:
A function formatting a tablature
note head.  Called with three arguments: context, string number and,
fret number.  It returns the text as a markup.

contextProperties.name: tempoCountPrecision
contextProperties.doc:
Rounding precision for
metronome rate.  Readers should use 1 as the default when this property is
not set.

contextProperties.name: tempoHideNote
contextProperties.doc: Hide the note = count in tempo marks.

contextProperties.name: tempoWholesPerMinute
contextProperties.doc:
The tempo in
whole notes per minute.

contextProperties.name: tieWaitForNote
contextProperties.doc:
If true, tied notes do not have to
follow each other directly.  This can be used for writing out
arpeggios.

contextProperties.name: timeSignature
contextProperties.doc:
A time-signature specification.  See
the `\time` command.

contextProperties.name: timeSignatureSettings
contextProperties.doc:
A nested alist of settings for
time signatures.  Contains elements for various time signatures.  The
element for each time signature contains entries for `beatBase`,
`beatStructure`, and `beamExceptions`.

contextProperties.name: timing
contextProperties.doc:
Keep administration of measure length,
position, bar number, etc.?  Switch off for cadenzas.

contextProperties.name: toeHeelStyle
contextProperties.doc:
The style for the glyph shape and behavior of
`\rtoe` and siblings.  Possible values are `default`,
`standard`, `reversed`, `circleheels`, and `below`.  If not
set (the default), use value `default`.

contextProperties.name: tonic
contextProperties.doc: The tonic of the current scale.

contextProperties.name: topLevelAlignment
contextProperties.doc:
If true, the *Vertical_align_engraver*
will create a *VerticalAlignment*; otherwise, it will create a
*StaffGrouper*

contextProperties.name: tupletFullLength
contextProperties.doc:
If set, the tuplet is printed up to
the start of the next note.

contextProperties.name: tupletFullLengthNote
contextProperties.doc:
If set, end at the next note,
otherwise end on the matter (time signatures, etc.) before the note.

contextProperties.name: tupletSpannerDuration
underlyingRepeatBarType
contextProperties.doc:
Bar line to insert at points
of repetition or departure where no bar line would normally appear,
for example at the end of a system broken in mid measure where the
next system begins with a segno.  Where there is also a repeat bar
line, the repeat bar line takes precedence and this value is appended
to it as an annotation.  The default is `||`.

contextProperties.name: useBassFigureExtenders
contextProperties.doc:
Whether to use extender lines
for repeated bass figures.

contextProperties.name: vocalName
contextProperties.doc: Name of a vocal line.

contextProperties.name: whichBar
contextProperties.doc:
The current bar line type, or `'()` if
there is no bar line.  Setting this explicitly in user code is
deprecated.  Use `\bar` or related commands to set it.
